labels.name: comp/dashboard
labels.description: Web dashboard / control panel UI (dashboard/, landing)

items.body: /Summary When the dashboard is bound to a non-loopback address (--host 0.0.0.0) and the only registered auth provider is a password-capable one (i.e. BasicAuthProvider), every unauthenticated HTML navigation to / returns HTTP 500 (Internal Server Error) instead of reaching the login page. The /login interstitial renders fine and password login itself works — only the root-path redirect is broken. What the user sees at / (the auto-SSO redirect lands on a route the provider cannot serve): What they should see (the /login interstitial, which renders the password form correctly): Version text Hermes Agent v0.18.0 (2026.7.1) · upstream 83016547 OpenAI SDK: 2.24.0 Reproduction Configure dashboard.basic_auth in config.yaml (and ensure no OAuth provider like Nous is registered): yaml dashboard: host: 0.0.0.0 port: 9119 basic_auth: username: admin password: "..." secret: "..." session_ttl_seconds: 43200 Launch the dashboard (built web UI present): bash hermes dashboard --host 0.0.0.0 --port 9119 --no-open --skip-build Confirm only one provider is registered: bash curl -s http://127.0.0.1:9119/api/auth/providers # {"providers":[{"name":"basic","display_name":"Username & Password","supports_password":true}]} Hit the root path: bash curl -i http://127.0.0.1:9119/ # HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error Expected GET / (unauthenticated HTML) → 302 to /login?next=%2F, rendering the password form. Actual GET / → 302 to /auth/login?provider=basic, which calls BasicAuthProvider.start_login(), which raises: text NotImplementedError: BasicAuthProvider is password-only; there is no OAuth redirect flow. The login page POSTs to /auth/password-login instead. → HTTP 500. Root cause _auto_sso_response() in hermes_cli/dashboard_auth/middleware.py triggers an automatic redirect to /auth/login?provider= whenever exactly one session provider is registered. It does not check whether that provider actually supports the OAuth redirect flow: python provider = providers[0] ... auth_login = f"{prefix}/auth/login?provider={quote(provider.name, safe='')}" For BasicAuthProvider, supports_password = True and start_login() / complete_login() both raise NotImplementedError (by design — see plugins/dashboard_auth/basic/__init__.py:229). So the auto-SSO redirect lands on a route the provider cannot serve. Suggested fix In _auto_sso_response(), skip the auto-SSO redirect for password-capable providers and fall through to the /login interstitial (which correctly renders the password form): diff provider = providers[0] + # A password-capable provider authenticates via POST /auth/password-login + # from the /login page — it has no OAuth redirect flow, so start_login() + # raises NotImplementedError. Fall through to the /login interstitial, + # which renders the password form for such providers. + if getattr(provider, "supports_password", False): + return None prefix = prefix_from_request(request) Workaround Access /login directly instead of /. The password form renders and login succeeds. Notes Regression window: the June 2026 hardening made a public bind require an auth provider, which pushed single-box self-hosted users toward basic_auth — making this the common path for that deployment shape. Verified the suggested fix locally: GET / → 302 /login?next=%2F, login + session flow all green, no errors in logs.

items.title: Kanban workers never receive the kanban_* toolset — _get_platform_tools drops check_fn-gated toolsets for platform cli

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Summary

Dispatcher-spawned kanban workers never receive the `kanban_*` lifecycle tools in their schema, contrary to [the kanban docs](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/kanban) ("The dispatcher spawns each worker with these tools already in its schema"). Workers spawn as generic agents with no worker protocol prompt and no `kanban_show`/`kanban_complete`, so they burn their iteration budget blindly exploring the workspace / sqlite DB, then exit → the dispatcher records `crashed: worker exited cleanly (rc=0) without calling kanban_complete or kanban_block — protocol violation`, and after `failure_limit` attempts the task auto-blocks. Every plain `kanban create` + dispatch fails this way out of the box.

Probably the same root cause as #52141 (orchestrator-mode variant).

## Environment

- Docker image built from `main` on 2026-07-07 (also reproduced on a 2026-06-23 build)
- Single default profile (`HERMES_HOME=/opt/data`), gateway-embedded dispatcher
- Platform: `cli` workers spawned as `hermes -p default chat -q "work kanban task <id>"`

## Repro

```bash
hermes kanban create "test" --body "mark this task complete with summary pong" --assignee default
# wait for dispatcher → task blocks after 2 runs with "protocol violation"

# direct probe:
HERMES_KANBAN_TASK=t_x hermes -p default chat -q "call the kanban_show tool"
# → model has no kanban_* tools in schema
```

## Diagnosis

The registry/gating layers all work:

```python
from toolsets import TOOLSETS, resolve_toolset
"kanban" in TOOLSETS                      # True
resolve_toolset("kanban")                 # 8 tools incl. kanban_show/complete/block
from tools.kanban_tools import _check_kanban_mode
_check_kanban_mode()                      # True (HERMES_KANBAN_TASK set)
```

But the per-platform assembly drops the toolset:

```python
from hermes_cli.tools_config import _get_platform_tools
_get_platform_tools(load_config(), "cli") # → no kanban toolset, ever
```

Reading `_get_platform_tools`:

1. With an explicit `platform_toolsets.cli` list, the explicit branch only honors `CONFIGURABLE_TOOLSETS` membership — `kanban` (check_fn-gated, non-configurable) is filtered out even when listed by hand.
2. The trailing "recover non-configurable platform toolsets" pass requires `ts_tools.issubset(platform_tool_universe)` where the universe is the platform composite (`hermes-cli`). The `kanban_*` tools are not part of any platform composite, so recovery always skips them.

Net effect: no code path can put `kanban` into a worker's toolsets for platform `cli`, regardless of `HERMES_KANBAN_TASK`, `platform_toolsets`, or the top-level `toolsets:` list. The `_check_kanban_mode()` env-var gate is never even consulted for schema assembly.

## Related paper cut

`kanban swarm` assigns `requesting-code-review` (verifier) and `humanizer` (synthesizer) skills to its cards. Both ship in the default `skills.disabled` list, and a card whose only requested skill is unavailable hard-fails at spawn (`ValueError: Unknown skill(s)` in cli.py) → verifier/synthesizer crash-loop until auto-block. Consider degrading to a warning when kanban-spawned, or not defaulting swarm cards to disabled-by-default skills.

## Workaround we're using

- `command_allowlist: ["hermes kanban *", "/opt/hermes/.venv/bin/hermes kanban *"]` so headless workers can shell out without approval prompts, plus an `AGENTS.md` dropped in each task workspace instructing: read your spec with `hermes kanban show <id>`, then close with `hermes kanban complete <id> --summary "..."`. With that in place, workers/swarms complete fine (CLI-complete satisfies the protocol watcher).

items.title: Cron delivery to Telegram silently dropped when user session is active on same chat

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

items.body:
## Summary

Cron jobs with `deliver: "origin"` (or explicit `deliver: "telegram:<chat_id>"`) log `"delivered to telegram:<chat_id> via live adapter"` in the agent log but the message **never reaches the Telegram API**. The gateway log shows zero trace of the send. This happens specifically when the target Telegram chat has an **active user session**.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start the gateway with a Telegram bot connected to a DM chat.
2. Create a `no_agent: true` cron job with `deliver: "origin"` pointing to that chat (script: `echo "test"`).
3. **Without an active session:** The cron fires → message arrives on Telegram ✅
4. **With an active session** (user sends a message, agent is processing): The cron fires → agent.log says `"delivered to telegram:<chat_id> via live adapter"` → **nothing arrives on Telegram** 🔴

## Evidence

**Cron at 08:02 (session active):**

agent.log:
```
2026-07-07 08:02:50,321 INFO cron.scheduler: Job '<id>': delivered to telegram:<chat_id> via live adapter
```

gateway.log — completely silent at 08:00–08:03. Zero entries. No Telegram API call logged.

**Test cron at 11:02 (session active, `no_agent: true`, trivial bash script):**
```bash
#!/bin/bash
echo "TEST CRON — $(date '+%H:%M:%S')"
```

agent.log:
```
2026-07-07 11:02:48,849 INFO cron.scheduler: Job '<id>': delivered to telegram:<chat_id>
```

gateway.log — again, **zero entries**.

**Early-morning crons (06:30–07:13, no user session):** All delivered successfully with matching gateway.log entries:
```
2026-07-07 06:31:22,092 INFO gateway.delivery: Cron output preserved for chunking adapter (4520 chars)
2026-07-07 07:03:26,445 INFO gateway.delivery: Cron output preserved for chunking adapter (4059 chars)
```

## Root Cause Analysis

The live-adapter delivery path in `_deliver_result` (`cron/scheduler.py:1228`) schedules the delivery coroutine on the gateway's event loop via `safe_schedule_threadsafe` → `asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe`. The coroutine goes through `DeliveryRouter._deliver_to_platform` → `adapter.send()`.

`future.result(timeout=60)` completes successfully (in ~200ms — too fast for an actual Telegram API call). `_confirm_adapter_delivery(send_result)` returns `True`. The scheduler logs "delivered via live adapter".

But the gateway event loop — busy with the active user session — either:
1. Executes a code path in the Telegram adapter that returns `SendResult(success=True)` without calling the Telegram API, or
2. Short-circuits because the adapter is in a streaming state for the user session.

The fact that `gateway.log` shows **zero** Telegram API calls for these deliveries, while all other cron deliveries (outside active sessions) DO appear, points to a false-positive success return.

**Reproduces with both `no_agent: true` and LLM-driven crons.**

## Workaround

Schedule crons to fire **before** the user typically starts messaging. Since early-morning deliveries work fine, moving from 08:00 to 07:56 avoids the active-session window.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.17.0 (2026.6.19) · upstream 4b9d9b20
- Python 3.11.15
- Linux (Hetzner VPS, Ubuntu)
- Telegram Bot API (DM)

## Impact

**P1 / data-loss bug.** Any user relying on cron jobs to deliver time-sensitive content to a Telegram chat they actively use will silently lose messages — morning briefings, alerts, scheduled reports — with no error, no retry, and misleading "delivered" confirmation in logs.

items.title: [Windows] installer stash-pop fails with merge conflict on website/i18n/zh-Hans docs files — blocks finalize stages on repeated runs

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:risk-platform-windows
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break or behave differently on native Windows

items.body:
## Problem

On Windows, running the installer more than once triggers a `git stash apply` failure due to a merge conflict in `website/i18n/zh-Hans/docusaurus-plugin-content-docs/current/reference/environment-variables.md`. The stash pop fails because upstream updated this file between installer runs, and the stash contains a modified version from a previous run.

From bootstrap log:
```
CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in website/i18n/zh-Hans/docusaurus-plugin-content-docs/current/reference/environment-variables.md
[X] Update succeeded, but restoring local changes failed. Your changes are still preserved in git stash.
-> Resolve manually with: git stash apply stash@{0}
{"skipped":false,"ok":false,"reason":"git stash apply failed after update","duration_ms":8287,"stage":"repository"}
```

## Root cause

The installer runs `git stash` before `git pull`, then `git stash pop` after. If upstream also modified `environment-variables.md` in the same window (which it did — 2+ commits landed during installation), the stash pop produces a merge conflict and the bootstrap aborts before any finalize stages run.

The affected file is documentation-only (not runtime code), so the merge conflict has no functional impact on `hermes` itself.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Run installer on Windows
2. Let it get partway through (packages install, then fail at baseline-imports check)
3. Run installer again — now stash contains the partial state from run 1, and upstream has new commits
4. Installer fails: `git stash apply failed after update`

## Expected

Installer should either:
- Use `git stash drop` instead of `git stash apply` for website/docs files (not runtime code)
- Or use `git stash pop --index` with a conflict resolution strategy that takes upstream for docs files: `git checkout --theirs website/i18n/ && git add website/i18n/`
- Or skip stashing `website/` entirely since it's never modified by hermes runtime

## Workaround

```bash
cd $LOCALAPPDATA/hermes/hermes-agent
git checkout --theirs website/i18n/zh-Hans/docusaurus-plugin-content-docs/current/reference/environment-variables.md
git add website/i18n/
git stash drop
```

## Environment

- OS: Windows 11 Enterprise 26200
- Hermes installer: `install-main.ps1` (repeated runs, 2026-07-08)
- Frequency: happens on every installer re-run during active upstream development

Thanks for the great work on Hermes Agent!

items.title: [Bug]: Hermes TUI assistant reply text remains low-contrast on macOS Terminal.app light profile

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
### Bug Description

Hermes TUI assistant reply text can still be difficult or impossible to read on macOS Terminal.app light profiles when Hermes is launched through the terminal path used by NemoClaw.

This is related to earlier light-theme/color issues, but the observed failure is narrower than a general theme-detection failure: the response panel chrome and "Hermes" label render, while the assistant reply body itself appears near-white/too faint against a light terminal background.

Related reports:

- NVIDIA/NemoClaw#6380 - macOS Terminal.app light profile, Hermes TUI reply box looks empty because the reply body is unreadable.
- #8526 - terminal light-theme colors not readable.
- #59751 - Hermes.app TUI reply text too faint on macOS Retina.
- #49082 - Apple_Terminal light/dark detection mismatch in the TypeScript TUI path.
- #30092 - OSC 11 probing hazards on macOS Terminal.app.

The current `ui-tui/src/theme.ts` `LIGHT_THEME` is already darker than the dark palette, but the default light palette still leans heavily on gold/brown values and pale surfaces. In Terminal.app's default light profile, that does not give enough practical contrast for long assistant body text.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. On macOS, open Terminal.app with the default light-background profile.
2. Start a Hermes sandbox via NemoClaw, or otherwise launch Hermes TUI in a terminal environment equivalent to:
   - `TERM_PROGRAM=Apple_Terminal`
   - light terminal background
   - Hermes Agent v0.17.0 observed in the NemoClaw repro
3. Run `hermes`.
4. Send `hello`.
5. Observe the assistant response panel.

### Expected Behavior

Assistant response body text should be readable on the default macOS Terminal.app light profile without requiring users to switch the whole terminal to a dark profile.

The default light palette should use a neutral high-contrast foreground for body text, with darker muted/label colors and slightly stronger panel/chrome contrast.

### Actual Behavior

The response panel border and label are visible, but the assistant reply body can render so faintly that the panel appears empty on a light terminal background.

### Affected Component

CLI (interactive chat)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

N/A (CLI only)

### Debug Report

Not available from the reporter environment. The issue is rendering-only; the agent response completes successfully and becomes visible after switching Terminal.app to a dark profile.

### Operating System

macOS Terminal.app light profile; remote/sandbox host in the NemoClaw repro was Ubuntu 24.04 aarch64.

### Python Version

Not captured for the upstream issue. NemoClaw repro used the npm Hermes wrapper and displayed Hermes Agent v0.17.0.

### Hermes Version

Hermes Agent v0.17.0 (2026.6.19) in the NemoClaw repro.

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

No traceback. Rendering-only issue.

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

Likely in the default light palette path in `ui-tui/src/theme.ts`.

The current light palette uses:

- `text: #3D2F13`
- `muted/sessionLabel/sessionBorder: #7A5A0F`
- `completion/status surfaces: #F5F5F5`

Those are better than the dark palette on white backgrounds, but still tie long body text and secondary text to a gold/brown ramp. The practical result in Terminal.app light mode is weaker readability than a neutral text ramp.

This issue is intentionally not proposing a new theme engine or a detection change. It is a small default palette adjustment.

### Proposed Fix (optional)

Try a revised default `LIGHT_THEME` with a neutral high-contrast body/text ramp and slightly calmer accent colors, for example:

- `text`: `#1F2933`
- `muted`: `#52616B`
- `label/sessionLabel/sessionBorder`: `#5B6472`
- `primary`: `#6F4E00`
- `accent`: `#8A4F12`
- `border`: `#6B4A1F`
- `completionBg/statusBg`: `#FAFAF7`
- current/selection backgrounds: low-saturation blue/amber tints rather than pale gold-only surfaces

Add/update `ui-tui/src/__tests__/theme.test.ts` assertions so the light palette keeps body text neutral/dark and does not regress back to near-white/gold-only foregrounds.

items.title: [comp/desktop] Desktop boot fails when platform adapter import or MCP registration exceeds the 15s readiness timeout

labels.name: comp/dashboard
labels.description: Web dashboard / control panel UI (dashboard/, landing)

items.body:
### Environment

- Hermes Agent version: v0.18.0 (commit 5eac6652, Electron build win-unpacked)
- OS: Windows 10 (native install, not WSL)
- Default install: 7 MCP servers + 21 bundled platform adapters
- Hermes CLI / Dashboard: work normally
- Hermes Desktop: boot fails on every launch

### Summary

Hermes Desktop on Windows fails to start with "Timed out connecting to Hermes backend after 15000ms". The backend reports HERMES_BACKEND_READY within ~5s and /api/health responds in <100 ms, but the Electron readiness probe waits for /api/status, which blocks for the full 15s window and then triggers the error dialog. The boot loop retries 4 times before giving up.

### Root cause

The 15 s budget is spent entirely inside /api/status -> load_gateway_config() -> platform_registry._resolve_all(), which eagerly imports every deferred platform adapter. On the default install with 21 platforms, this takes 12-13 s on first call. Adding register_mcp_servers() on top makes the first-request budget roughly 24 s. The CLI and Dashboard never hit /api/status at startup, so they are unaffected.

Measured on this machine (cProfile + stopwatch):

- register_mcp_servers(7 servers): 23.91 s first call
- load_gateway_config(): 12.83 s first call
- platform_registry.plugin_entries() (21 plugins): 12.36 s of that 12.83 s
- yaml.safe_load(config.yaml, 18 KB): 0.09 s
- discover_plugins(): 1.05 s

After deleting 19 of 21 platform plugin folders (keeping only telegram/) /api/status responds in 3 s and Desktop starts cleanly. There is no config knob to achieve the same effect without deleting files.

### Suggested fixes (any one would unblock the user)

1. Make the Desktop timeout configurable. apps/desktop/electron/hardening.cjs hardcodes DEFAULT_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS = 15_000. Read it from env HERMES_DESKTOP_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS or from config.yaml under desktop.fetch_timeout_ms. Smallest change, pure escape hatch.

2. Honor plugins.disabled / platforms.<name>.enabled: false in the cold-start path. gateway/config.py:_apply_env_overrides() and platform_registry._resolve_all() need to consult _get_disabled_plugins() (already correctly read in hermes_cli/plugins.py:180) before importing each deferred adapter. The Slack fix from commit 156176a44 (the _enable_from_env helper plus _enabled_explicit marker) is the pattern -- it just has not been migrated to Discord, Telegram, etc. Without this, even users who explicitly disable a platform in config.yaml still pay its 0.5-2 s import cost.

3. Defer cold-start work past the readiness probe. /api/status should return "process is up, uvicorn is listening" in <1 s. The heavy register_mcp_servers + load_gateway_config should run in a background coroutine after HERMES_BACKEND_READY is emitted; the renderer polls a separate /api/tools/ready endpoint. This is the only fix that scales -- users with 10 MCP servers and 5 enabled platforms will eventually hit the timeout even with #1 and #2 in place.

A useful intermediate for #3: there is already _warm_gateway_module() in hermes_cli/web_server.py:157 running in run_in_executor. Adding one extra load_gateway_config() call inside it (after the existing import hermes_cli.gateway) is a 5-line patch that immediately fixes this user's case.

### Workaround that worked for me

Deleted 19 of 21 platform folders under plugins/platforms/, kept only telegram/. Backup at temp-files/platforms-backup-20260707_124044.zip. /api/status returned in 3 s, Desktop started. Must be repeated after every hermes update because update restores the deleted folders. Until #1 lands, the safer workaround is the env var HERMES_DESKTOP_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS=90000.

### Related issues

- #54928 same symptom, attributes it to slow model load
- #48504 same DEFAULT_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS root cause on /api/profiles
- #53130 voice transcription timeout on first faster-whisper load (same timeout)
- #31109, #32058 hermes plugins disable platforms/<x> and platforms.<name>.enabled: false are silently ignored
- #55113 Telegram env-override-wins bug; Slack-style fix in commit 156176a44 not yet migrated
- #45435 Git for Windows detection mismatch in bootstrap vs ensureRuntime

### Logs tail

%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\logs\desktop.log (i.e. C:\Users\User\AppData\Local\hermes\logs\desktop.log on Windows) repeats 4x:

    [boot] HERMES_BACKEND_READY port=50207
    [boot] Waiting for Hermes backend to become ready
    [boot] Desktop boot failed: Hermes backend did not become ready: Timed out connecting to Hermes backend after 15000ms
    [boot] Restarting desktop connection
    Hermes backend exited (1)
    [boot] Hermes backend exited before it became ready (1).

items.title: MOA does not pass extra_body parameters to reference model API calls

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
## Bug Description

The Mixture-of-Agents (MOA) system does not pass `extra_body` parameters from `custom_providers` configuration to the actual API calls made to reference models.

This prevents using reasoning models (like Qwen3.7-max with `enable_thinking` or LongCat-2.0 with `thinking`) as MOA reference models, because these models return a non-standard `reasoning_content` field that MOA cannot parse.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Add a reasoning model (e.g., Qwen3.7-max) to `custom_providers` with `extra_body`:
   ```yaml
   custom_providers:
     - name: dashscope
       base_url: https://ws-a9s7j6wb08qbbv27.cn-beijing.maas.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1
       api_key: ${DASHSCOPE_API_KEY}
       model: qwen3.7-max
       extra_body:
         enable_thinking: false
   ```

2. Add this provider to MOA `reference_models`:
   ```yaml
   moa:
     presets:
       default:
         reference_models:
           - provider: dashscope
             model: qwen3.7-max
   ```

3. Trigger MOA with `/moa <question>`

4. MOA hangs or skips the model (because `enable_thinking` is not passed, so the model returns `reasoning_content` which MOA cannot parse)

## Expected Behavior

MOA should pass `extra_body` parameters to the model API call, allowing reasoning models to work with thinking disabled.

## Actual Behavior

- MOA hangs when calling Qwen3.7-max (with `extra_body` configured)
- MOA silently skips LongCat-2.0 (returns `reasoning_content`)

## Verification

Direct API call with `enable_thinking: false` works correctly:
```bash
curl -s --max-time 10 'https://ws-a9s7j6wb08qbbv27.cn-beijing.maas.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1/chat/completions'   -H 'Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY'   -H 'Content-Type: application/json'   -d '{"model":"qwen3.7-max","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hello"}],"max_tokens":50,"enable_thinking":false}'
```

Returns standard OpenAI format (no `reasoning_content`):
```json
{
  "choices": [{
    "message": {
      "role": "assistant",
      "content": "Hello!"
    }
  }]
}
```

## Environment

- **Hermes Agent version:** v0.18.0 (2026.7.1) · upstream 605727e3
- **Python:** 3.11.15
- **OpenAI SDK:** 2.24.0
- **OS:** Ubuntu (Linux 6.17.0-29-generic)
- **MOA models affected:** Qwen3.7-max, LongCat-2.0

## Additional Context

This affects models from:
- Alibaba DashScope (Qwen3.5/3.6/3.7 series with `enable_thinking`)
- Meituan LongCat (with `thinking` parameter)

These models are widely used in China and returning `reasoning_content` by default is becoming standard behavior for many LLM providers.

items.title: [Bug]: GET /api/sessions/{id}/messages has no pagination — loads entire transcript at once, freezes Desktop on large sessions

labels.name: comp/dashboard
labels.description: Web dashboard / control panel UI (dashboard/, landing)

items.body:
# Reproduction: `getSessionMessages()` loads entire transcript at once — no pagination

## Bug Description

When the Desktop (or any client) calls `GET /api/sessions/{id}/messages`, the endpoint returns **all** messages for that session in a single response with no pagination parameters. For sessions with 500+ messages, this produces 1.2–1.6 MB JSON payloads that are loaded entirely into memory on both the backend (serialization) and frontend (parsing + Zustand store).

Under GIL pressure from concurrent agent turns, this synchronous SQLite read + JSON serialization amplifies event-loop starvation, contributing directly to the `ws write slow (loop stalled >10.0s)` → `WebSocketDisconnect` cascade documented in #53773, #48445, and #50005.

## Evidence

### 1. Backend endpoint has ZERO pagination parameters

**File:** `hermes_cli/web_server.py:8105-8116`
```python
@app.get("/api/sessions/{session_id}/messages")
async def get_session_messages(session_id: str, profile: Optional[str] = None):
    db = _open_session_db_for_profile(profile)
    try:
        sid = db.resolve_session_id(session_id)
        sid = db.resolve_resume_session_id(sid)
        messages = db.get_messages(sid)
        return {"session_id": sid, "messages": messages}
    finally:
        db.close()
```

No `limit`, `offset`, `page`, `min_messages`, or `order` parameters. Every call dumps the entire conversation.

### 2. Desktop frontend passes no pagination

**File:** `apps/desktop/src/hermes.ts:295-302`
```typescript
export function getSessionMessages(id: string, profile?: string | null): Promise<SessionMessagesResponse> {
  const suffix = profile ? `?profile=${encodeURIComponent(profile)}` : ''
  return window.hermesDesktop.api<SessionMessagesResponse>({
    ...(profile ? { profile } : {}),
    path: `/api/sessions/${encodeURIComponent(id)}/messages${suffix}`
  })
}
```

### 3. Contrast with session list endpoints

`GET /api/sessions` supports pagination:
```python
async def get_sessions(
    limit: int = 20, offset: int = 0, min_messages: int = 0,
    archived: str = "exclude", order: str = "created",
    source: str = None, exclude_sources: str = None,
    cwd_prefix: str = None, profile: Optional[str] = None,
):
```

But `GET /api/sessions/{id}/messages` has none of these.

### 4. Actual payload sizes (production state.db)

Measured on a real Hermes Desktop installation (Windows 10, Hermes v0.18.0):

```
Session ID                           Messages  Raw Content  JSON Payload
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
20260707_102815_c4d80b               518        1.39 MB      1.51 MB
20260707_034747_43cdb6               703        1.19 MB      1.29 MB
20260707_124712_48881d               139        0.55 MB      0.58 MB
```

Three sessions alone require **~3.4 MB** of JSON to be serialized from SQLite, sent over HTTP, parsed by the frontend, and stored in React state — all in a single blocking operation.

### 5. How this compounds GIL starvation

The endpoint is `async def`, so it runs on the asyncio event loop. Under GIL pressure:
- `db.get_messages(sid)` holds the GIL while reading all rows from SQLite
- JSON serialization of the response dict holds the GIL
- The event loop cannot process WebSocket writes during this time
- If an agent turn is already holding the GIL, the endpoint waits — and times out

This creates a feedback loop:
```
Agent processing → GIL contention → API call slow → WS write timeout
→ Desktop disconnect → reconnect → loads same session → same cycle
```

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Have a Hermes Desktop session with 500+ messages (~1MB+ content)
2. Open the Desktop app and click on that session in the sidebar
3. Observe the timeline:
   - `desktop-controller.tsx:509` calls `getSessionMessages(storedSessionId)`
   - This triggers `GET /api/sessions/{id}/messages`
   - The backend loads ALL 500+ messages from SQLite
   - Serializes ~1.4 MB of JSON
   - Under agent load, this operation takes 5-30 seconds
   - WebSocket write buffer stalls → `ws write slow (loop stalled >10.0s)`
4. The Desktop UI shows a loading spinner but may time out

## Expected Behavior

The messages endpoint should support pagination (at minimum `limit` and `offset`) so clients can load messages in chunks. The desktop's `hydrateFromStoredSession` should load messages incrementally, with the most recent first, similar to how the session list (`listAllProfileSessions`) already paginates.

## Environment

- **OS:** Windows 10
- **Hermes:** v0.18.0 (2026.7.1), upstream 83016547
- **Python:** 3.11.15
- **Desktop:** Electron (local TUI gateway via WebSocket)
- **Provider:** deepseek-v4-flash via opencode-go

## Related Issues

- #53773 — TUI WebSocket disconnects during long-running delegate_task
- #48445 — Desktop gateway WebSocket disconnects during long foreground tasks
- #50005 — WS disconnect / GIL starvation (closed, fixed partial)
- #56888 — setup.runtime_check missing from _LONG_HANDLERS (#50005 residual)

## Proposed Fix

1. Add `limit`, `offset`, and `order` query parameters to `GET /api/sessions/{id}/messages`
2. Default to `limit=50, order=desc` (most recent first — what the virtual list renders)
3. Modify `hydrateFromStoredSession` in `desktop-controller.tsx` to load messages in batches
4. Consider returning a `total` count alongside the page so the virtual list knows its height

items.title: Dangerous-command approval deadlock on worker threads still unfixed in v0.18.0 (re: #15216 / PR #16477)

items.body:
## Summary
On Hermes Agent v0.18.0 (2026.7.1, upstream `536ffed`) a dangerous/sudo command
triggered from a worker thread hangs for 10+ minutes with no approval prompt the
user can reach — even though a live `prompt_toolkit` TUI owns the terminal. This
is the exact regression described in #15216, and the fix landed in PR #16477
(`run_in_terminal`), but **v0.18.0's `tools/approval.py` still contains the old
fail-closed guard**, not the `run_in_terminal` path.

I confirmed `git log origin/main` (fetched 2026-07-07, `aaeba21`) shows **no**
commit referencing `16477` / `run_in_terminal` / `15216` / `stdin deadlock`, so
the fix does not appear to be in `main` either.

## Reproduction (real logs from this box)
`~/.hermes/logs/errors.log` (approx. line 5678):
```
WARNING tools.approval: Dangerous-command approval requested on a thread with
no approval callback while prompt_toolkit is active; denying to avoid stdin
deadlock. command='<external network command>'
```

User-visible symptom (from a session debug log): the agent process appeared to
hang for roughly 15 minutes with no approval prompt the user could reach; the
user reported having no approval entry point to click. This matches the
reported behavior in #15216.

## Root cause
`prompt_dangerous_approval` spawns a background-thread `input()` when no approval
callback is registered on the calling thread. A worker thread
(`ThreadPoolExecutor`, e.g. concurrent tool dispatch) does not inherit the CLI's
`threading.local()` approval callback, so it falls back to `input()` while
`prompt_toolkit` owns stdin -> keystrokes never reach the reader -> invisible
deadlock. The old code fail-closed with `return "deny"` + warning, so the command
just hangs waiting for an approval dialog that never renders (and on the messaging
gateway the dialog only renders in the CLI terminal anyway).

## Proposed fix (verified locally)
Route the fallback prompt through `prompt_toolkit.Application.run_in_terminal`,
which detaches the TUI's stdin reader and restores cooked mode so `input()` works
from the worker thread. Full diff below; I've run a focused `unittest` (module
import + no-live-app returns None + callback fast-path + integration test that
stubs a live TUI and asserts the helper is actually reached, not `TypeError`-
swallowed). Restarted `hermes-gateway`, deadlock gone.

```diff
```diff
diff --git a/tools/approval.py b/tools/approval.py
index c686685..b11c045 100644
--- a/tools/approval.py
+++ b/tools/approval.py
@@ -1659,6 +1659,72 @@ def save_permanent_allowlist(patterns: set):
 # Approval prompting + orchestration
 # =========================================================================
 
+def _try_pt_run_in_terminal_prompt(display_command: str,
+                                   display_description: str,
+                                   timeout_seconds: int | None,
+                                   allow_permanent: bool) -> str | None:
+    """Route a blocking approval prompt through prompt_toolkit's
+    run_in_terminal so a background thread can read stdin without
+    deadlocking the live TUI (issue #15216 / PR #16477).
+
+    When a live prompt_toolkit Application owns the TTY, calling input()
+    from a worker thread competes with the TUI's stdin reader and the
+    keystrokes never reach the reader -> invisible deadlock. run_in_terminal
+    detaches the TUI's stdin reader and restores cooked mode for the duration
+    of the callable, so input() below actually receives the user's choice.
+
+    Returns 'once'/'session'/'always'/'deny', or None when no live
+    prompt_toolkit Application is active (caller falls back to legacy path).
+    """
+    try:
+        from prompt_toolkit.application.current import get_app_or_none
+        from prompt_toolkit.application.run_in_terminal import run_in_terminal
+        from agent.i18n import t
+    except Exception:
+        return None
+
+    app = get_app_or_none()
+    if app is None:
+        return None
+
+    import asyncio
+    import time
+
+    def _render_and_read():
+        try:
+            print()
+            print(f"  {t('approval.dangerous_header', description=display_description)}")
+            print(f"      {display_command}")
+            print()
+            if allow_permanent:
+                print(t("approval.choose_long"))
+            else:
+                print(t("approval.choose_short"))
+            print()
+            sys.stdout.flush()
+            prompt = t("approval.prompt_long") if allow_permanent else t("approval.prompt_short")
+            raw = input(prompt).strip().lower()
+        except (EOFError, OSError):
+            raw = ""
+        choice = raw
+        if choice in {'o', 'once'}:
+            return 'once'
+        elif choice in {'s', 'session'}:
+            return 'session'
+        elif choice in {'a', 'always'}:
+            return 'always' if allow_permanent else 'session'
+        return 'deny'
+
+    async def _schedule():
+        return await app.run_in_terminal(_render_and_read)
+
+    try:
+        future = asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe(_schedule(), app.loop)
+        return future.result(timeout=timeout_seconds or 60)
+    except Exception:
+        return "deny"
+
+
 def prompt_dangerous_approval(command: str, description: str,
                               timeout_seconds: int | None = None,
                               allow_permanent: bool = True,
@@ -1694,31 +1760,29 @@ def prompt_dangerous_approval(command: str, description: str,
             logger.error("Approval callback failed: %s", e, exc_info=True)
             return "deny"
 
-    # Fail-closed guard: if prompt_toolkit owns the terminal (interactive
-    # CLI session) and no approval callback is registered on this thread,
-    # the input() fallback below would spawn a daemon thread whose read
-    # can never see Enter -- the user's keystrokes go to prompt_toolkit,
-    # not input(), producing an invisible 60s deadlock (issue #15216).
-    # Deny fast and log loudly instead so the caller can surface a real
-    # error to the agent. Any thread that needs interactive approval must
-    # install a callback via tools.terminal_tool.set_approval_callback()
-    # before reaching this point (see delegate_tool.py, run_agent.py
-    # _execute_tool_calls_concurrent / _spawn_background_review for the
-    # established pattern).
+    # If prompt_toolkit owns the terminal (interactive CLI session) and no
+    # approval callback is registered on this thread, the legacy input()
+    # fallback would spawn a daemon thread whose read can never see Enter --
+    # the user's keystrokes go to prompt_toolkit, producing an invisible
+    # deadlock (issue #15216). Instead of denying outright, route the
+    # prompt through prompt_toolkit's run_in_terminal, which detaches the
+    # TUI's stdin reader and restores cooked mode so input() actually reads
+    # the user's keystrokes. Falls back to the legacy input() path only when
+    # no live prompt_toolkit Application is present (non-TUI: scripts, tests,
+    # sshd, etc.). Any thread that needs the callback path should install one
+    # via tools.terminal_tool.set_approval_callback() (see run_agent.py
+    # _execute_tool_calls_concurrent).
     try:
-        from prompt_toolkit.application.current import get_app_or_none
-        if get_app_or_none() is not None:
-            logger.warning(
-                "Dangerous-command approval requested on a thread with no "
-                "approval callback while prompt_toolkit is active; denying "
-                "to avoid stdin deadlock. command=%r description=%r",
-                command, description,
-            )
-            return "deny"
+        routed = _try_pt_run_in_terminal_prompt(
+            display_command=command,
+            display_description=description,
+            timeout_seconds=timeout_seconds,
+            allow_permanent=allow_permanent,
+        )
+        if routed is not None:
+            return routed
     except Exception:
-        # prompt_toolkit not installed, or detection failed -- fall through
-        # to the legacy input() path (safe in non-TUI contexts: scripts,
-        # tests, sshd, etc.).
+        # Detection failed -- fall through to the legacy input() path below.
         pass
 
     os.environ["HERMES_SPINNER_PAUSE"] = "1"

```
```

## Suggested follow-ups
1. Merge the `run_in_terminal` path into `main` (PR #16477 appears stalled/not merged).
2. Consider surfacing the approval request to the gateway chat even when the agent
   process is a CLI/TUI session, so gateway users aren't stranded with "no place to
   click Allow".

Environment: Linux 6.12, Python 3.11, prompt_toolkit 3.0.52, Hermes Agent v0.18.0.

LABELS: bug, approval, deadlock

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

items.body:
## Problem

When calling `/exit`, multiple MCP server tasks emit **ignored exceptions**:

```
Exception ignored in: <coroutine object MCPServerTask.run at 0x77c6b17a7cd0>
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/tmp/hp/tools/mcp_tool.py", line 2590, in run
    parked = await self._wait_for_reconnect_or_shutdown(...)
  File "/tmp/hp/tools/mcp_tool.py", line 1884, in _wait_for_reconnect_or_shutdown
    t.cancel()
  File ".../python3.12/asyncio/base_events.py", line 799, in call_soon
    self._check_closed()
  File ".../python3.12/asyncio/base_events.py", line 545, in _check_closed
    raise RuntimeError('Event loop is closed')
RuntimeError: Event loop is closed
```

## Root Cause

The shutdown sequence closes the asyncio event loop, but MCP tasks still running in `_wait_for_reconnect_or_shutdown` call `t.cancel()` → `call_soon()`. The loop is already closed, so `call_soon()` raises `RuntimeError`.

## Fix

Move `t.cancel()` **inside the try block** so the RuntimeError is caught:

```diff
 finally:
     for t in (shutdown_task, reconnect_task):
         if not t.done():
-            t.cancel()
             try:
+                t.cancel()
                 await t
-            except (asyncio.CancelledError, Exception):
+            except (asyncio.CancelledError, RuntimeError):
+                # RuntimeError: Event loop is closed during /exit
                 pass
```

This fix applies to **two locations** in `tools/mcp_tool.py`:
- Line ~1838 (keepalive loop)
- Line ~1881 (`_wait_for_reconnect_or_shutdown`)

## Impact

- **Functional**: Zero. `Exception ignored` means Python caught it and exited cleanly. No data loss.
- **Cosmetic**: Ugly noise in terminal on every `/exit`.

## Version

Hermes Agent v0.18.0 (2026.7.1)

items.title: [Bug]: delegate_task children hang at first API call after days of gateway uptime; process restart restores

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
## Summary

After the gateway process has been running for several days, **every async `delegate_task` child hangs indefinitely before completing its first model API call** (0 output tokens, no error, `child_timeout_seconds` never reaps it). Restarting the gateway fully restores delegation — an identical test child then completes in seconds. This looks like per-process state degradation rather than a deterministic bug, and it silently disables sisters/swarm/fan-out for users running a long-lived gateway.

Possibly related to #45496 (children hanging on tool calls) and #10364 (generic tool stall), but the signature here is narrower: the hang is at the child's **first chat completion**, affects **all providers**, and is **cured by a process restart**.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.18.0 (2026.7.1), upstream `4b9d9b20`
- Python 3.11.15, OpenAI SDK 2.24.0, aarch64 Linux (Ubuntu, Oracle Cloud VM)
- Gateway run via systemd, uptime ~3.5 days at time of hang
- Default model `gpt-5.5` via `openai-codex`; also reproduced with `nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b:free` via `openrouter` after pinning `delegation.model`

## Reproduction / evidence

On the degraded process (5 children, 2 providers, same day — all identical):

1. Any top-level agent turn calls `delegate_task` (single task, `role='coder'`).
2. Dispatch succeeds: `tools.async_delegation: Dispatched async delegation batch deleg_…`
3. Child session logs `agent.turn_context: conversation turn: session=… platform=subagent history=0`
4. **openai-codex children** additionally log `chat_completion_helpers: Disabling openai-codex no-byte TTFB watchdog for large request (~28k tokens) … Waiting for backend response` — then nothing, ever.
5. **openrouter children** log nothing after `turn_context` — no `API call #1` line at all.
6. Child rows stay `message_count=1, output_tokens=0`, no `end_reason`, for 45+ minutes; `delegation.child_timeout_seconds=600` does not fire.
7. A direct `curl` to the same OpenRouter endpoint at the same moment answers normally — the backend is fine; the subagent execution path is stuck.

After `systemctl restart` of the gateway (no config changes):

8. An identical `delegate_task` test completes normally — child on `nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b:free` produced 137 output tokens with the correct answer within ~2 minutes of dispatch.

Historical note: delegate children on this install completed normally in late June; the hang was first observed after the process had accumulated multi-day uptime in July.

## Suspicions (unverified)

- Per-thread persistent event-loop machinery used by worker threads (`model_tools.py` comment: delegate_task ThreadPoolExecutor threads use "a per-thread persistent loop") accumulating unusable loop/client state in long-lived daemon executor threads.
- The child-timeout not reaping suggests the child thread is blocked somewhere the timeout doesn't cover (before/inside the first completion await).

## Impact

- All background fan-out (top-level `delegate_task` is always background by design) silently produces nothing.
- No error surfaces anywhere — the parent gets a normal "dispatched" payload and the user simply never receives child results, so this can go unnoticed for weeks (it did here).

## Workarounds

- Restart the gateway process (fully restores delegation).
- We added a watchdog that alerts when a delegate-child session sits >15 min with 0 output tokens and no end_reason.

Happy to provide more logs or run diagnostics on request.

# Windows: `hermes update` always aborts — concurrent-instance guard detects its own venv launcher shim

**Environment:** Windows 10 Pro (10.0.19045), native install (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes`), Python 3.11.15, observed on v0.14.0 and still present after updating to v0.18.0 (`7e7e3af5`).

## Symptom

Every `hermes update` invoked through the normal launcher aborts:

```
✗ Another hermes.exe is running:
    PID 18152  hermes.exe
  Updating now would fail to overwrite ...\venv\Scripts\hermes.exe because
  Windows blocks REPLACE on a running executable.
```

The reported PID is different on every attempt and the process no longer exists moments later — because it is the update's **own launcher**.

## Root cause

`bin\hermes.cmd` runs `venv\Scripts\hermes.exe` (the console-script shim), which stays alive as the **parent** of the actual `python.exe`. `_detect_concurrent_hermes_instances` (hermes_cli/main.py, ~L7256) excludes only `os.getpid()` — the python.exe — so the guard always finds the invoker's own shim and exits 2.

## Repro

1. Native Windows install via the PowerShell one-liner.
2. `hermes update` (no other hermes processes running; verified via `Get-CimInstance Win32_Process`).
3. Always blocked; reported PID vanishes immediately after abort.

## Workaround

Invoke the updater without the shim:
`& "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\hermes\hermes-agent\venv\Scripts\python.exe" -c "import sys; sys.argv=['hermes','update','--yes']; from hermes_cli.main import main; main()"` (run with cwd inside the managed checkout — see related issue on PROJECT_ROOT/cwd).

## Suggested fix

Exclude the current process's ancestor chain (e.g. walk `psutil.Process().parents()` and drop their PIDs from `matches`), or compare against the shim path *plus* creation-time-vs-self heuristics. A regression test could assert that a detector run from under a shim whose exe matches `shim_paths` returns `[]`.

# Post-update lazy-backend refresh fails on stale `__pycache__` — cache is cleared one update too late

**Environment:** Windows 10, native install, updating v0.14.0 (`43c7a1b`, 2026-05-19) → v0.18.0 (`7e7e3af5`) — a 5,559-commit jump.

## Symptom

At the end of a successful `hermes update` (git pull + pip install OK), the lazy-backend refresh step failed for 4 of 17 backends:

```
→ Refreshing 17 active lazy backend(s)...
  ✓ 12 already current
  ⚠ provider.vertex failed to refresh: cannot import name 'apply_subprocess_home_env' from 'hermes_constants' (...\hermes_constants.py)
  ⚠ platform.telegram failed to refresh: (same)
  ⚠ platform.discord failed to refresh: (same)
  ⚠ platform.teams failed to refresh: (same)
```

`apply_subprocess_home_env` exists in the freshly pulled `hermes_constants.py` — the refresh subprocess imported **stale bytecode**. Running `hermes update` a second time printed:

```
  ✓ Cleared 42 stale __pycache__ directories
  ↑ 4 refreshed: provider.vertex, platform.telegram, platform.discord, platform.teams
```

…and everything succeeded. So the pycache-clearing step exists, but runs on the *next* update rather than before the backend refresh of the *current* one.

## Impact

After any large update, messaging platforms (telegram/discord/teams) can be left on their previous version with a scary warning, until the user happens to update again. On an unattended box this silently delays platform fixes.

## Suggested fix

Move/duplicate the stale-`__pycache__` sweep to run immediately after `git pull` + dependency install and **before** `→ Refreshing N active lazy backend(s)`, or launch refresh subprocesses with `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1` + `-B` and a cleared cache.

items.title: Feature: conditional LLM invocation from no-agent cron scripts

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Problem

No-agent cron scripts (`no_agent=True`) run deterministically and deliver stdout verbatim. But there's no way to conditionally wake up the LLM only when the script finds something worth evaluating.

Current options:
- `no_agent=True`: script runs, stdout delivered. Zero cost when healthy. But no LLM sanity-check on alerts — raw output hits the user directly, including false alarms.
- `no_agent=False` (default): LLM wakes up every tick, script output injected as context. LLM can filter false alarms. But costs tokens every tick even when the script found nothing.

What's missing: script runs first → if stdout is non-empty, LLM wakes up to evaluate → if empty, stay silent with zero token cost.

## Proposed Solution

A cron job mode where the script runs first, and the LLM is only spawned if the script produces non-empty stdout. Something like:

```yaml
no_agent: conditional  # or: script_gates_agent: true
```

When the script outputs nothing → silent, no LLM spawned (like no_agent=True).
When the script outputs something → LLM spawns with the script output as context (like default mode).

## Use Case

Cluster health monitoring: a deterministic Python script checks nodes, pods, PVCs, Longhorn volumes every 4h. When healthy, output is empty — zero cost. When issues are found, the LLM wakes up to evaluate whether they're real concerns or false alarms (e.g., static pods with moderate restart counts on recently-added nodes), and can patch the script to exclude that pattern in the future.

Currently the only workaround is having the script shell out to `hermes chat -q`, but that spawns a process that isn't a natural child of the harness — no memory injection, no session context, no proper toolset scoping, no delivery handling.

When a dangerous command triggers the approval flow, the approval.request event correctly reaches the desktop app and the $approvalRequest atom is properly set, but the approval bar ("Run / Reject" buttons) is never rendered in the transcript.

Steps to Reproduce
From a Hermes desktop chat session, ask the agent to run a command that triggers approval (e.g. rm xxx)
Agent thread blocks in _await_gateway_decision()
Desktop app receives approval.request event → setApprovalRequest() is called
PendingToolApproval component (approval.tsx:50-58) re-renders via useStore($approvalRequest), condition passes, should render <InlineApprovalBar>
Actual result: No approval bar appears in the UI at all
Expected Behavior
PendingToolApproval should render an inline approval bar with "Run / Reject" buttons below the tool row (or PendingApprovalFallback should show a floating bar).

Code Trace
Full chain verified:

tui_gateway/server.py:1261-1263 — register_gateway_notify(key, lambda data: _emit_approval_request(sid, data)) ✅ callback registered
tui_gateway/server.py:1004-1016 — _emit_approval_request sends JSON-RPC event ✅
apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-message-stream/gateway-event.ts:446-477 — receives approval.request, calls setApprovalRequest() ✅
apps/desktop/src/store/prompts.ts:93-94 — $approvalRequest atom written ✅
apps/desktop/src/components/assistant-ui/tool/approval.tsx:50-58 — PendingToolApproval subscribes via useStore($approvalRequest) ✅
apps/desktop/src/components/assistant-ui/tool/fallback.tsx:469 — {isPending && <PendingToolApproval part={part} />} mount point ✅
Suspected root cause: The React re-render triggered by useStore($approvalRequest) is blocked by @assistant-ui/react's rendering pipeline optimization — the component returns null on the first render, and the second render's DOM insertion never takes effect.

Environment
Hermes desktop app (Electron)
Windows 10
Approval triggered via terminal / execute_code tools

items.title: [Bug]: hermes --yolo broken — approval bypass silently ignored since v0.11.0

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

items.body:
## Bug Description

Starting `hermes --yolo` no longer bypasses dangerous command and Tirith security approval prompts. The `--yolo` flag is silently ignored — every command that the safety scanner flags still pops up a manual approval prompt, exactly as if YOLO mode was never enabled.

This is an import-time race condition. `HERMES_YOLO_MODE` is set inside the `cmd_chat()` function body (main.py ~line 2327), but `_prepare_agent_startup()` is called earlier from `main()` (the call site is at main.py ~line 14102, while the `cmd_chat(args)` call site is at ~line 14131). `_prepare_agent_startup()` invokes `discover_plugins()`, which triggers the import chain `tools.registry` → `tools.terminal_tool` → `tools.approval`. At that point `tools.approval` is imported and `_YOLO_MODE_FROZEN` is frozen from `os.getenv("HERMES_YOLO_MODE")` — which is still empty. By the time `cmd_chat()` sets the env var, the constant has already been frozen to `False`.

The freeze itself is intentional security design (PR #7994 — prevents prompt-injected skills from flipping the bypass mid-session). The bug is that the CLI entry point doesn't guarantee the env var is set before the first import of `tools.approval`.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Ensure Tirith is installed (`~/.hermes/bin/tirith` exists) — otherwise the bug is hidden because `check_command_security()` fails open when tirith is absent.
2. Start Hermes with YOLO mode:
   ```
   hermes --yolo
   ```
3. Ask the agent to run any command flagged by Tirith or `detect_dangerous_command`, e.g.:
   ```
   gh pr view 123 --json state | python3 -c "import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin))"
   ```
4. A manual approval prompt appears: "Security scan — [HIGH] Pipe to interpreter ..."

## Expected Behavior

`--yolo` should bypass **all** dangerous command approval prompts. Per `hermes --help`: "Bypass all dangerous command approval prompts". The command should execute without any prompt.

## Actual Behavior

The approval prompt appears despite `--yolo` being active. `_YOLO_MODE_FROZEN` is `False` because `tools.approval` was imported before `HERMES_YOLO_MODE` was set, so the YOLO early-return at approval.py:2331 is never taken, and execution falls through to the Tirith scan + dangerous command detection layer.

## Affected Component

- CLI (interactive chat)
- Tools (terminal, code execution)

## Messaging Platform

N/A (CLI only)

## Debug Report

https://paste.rs/XbLpY

(Feishu channel IDs redacted from gateway logs; all API keys auto-redacted by `hermes debug share`.)

## Operating System

Linux 6.18.36-amd64-desktop-rolling x86_64

## Python Version

3.11.15

## Hermes Version

v0.18.0 (2026.7.1, upstream 7426c09b)

## Root Cause Analysis

**Startup call sequence in `main()`:**

```
main()
  args = parser.parse_args(...)
  │
  ├── _prepare_agent_startup(args)              ← called at ~line 14102
  │     discover_plugins()
  │       PluginManager._load_plugin()
  │         from tools.registry import registry   # triggers import chain
  │           tools.terminal_tool
  │             tools.approval        ← _YOLO_MODE_FROZEN frozen HERE (env var still unset)
  │
  ├── ... (other startup steps)
  │
  └── cmd_chat(args)                            ← called at ~line 14131
        os.environ["HERMES_YOLO_MODE"] = "1"  ← TOO LATE (function body ~line 2327)
```

`_YOLO_MODE_FROZEN` is frozen once at module import time (approval.py:33) and never re-read. The env var is set afterwards in `cmd_chat()`, so the constant stays `False` for the entire process lifetime.

**All 3 approval paths affected** (each checks `_YOLO_MODE_FROZEN`):
- `check_all_command_guards()` — approval.py:2331 (terminal tool)
- `check_execute_code_guard()` — approval.py:2733 (execute_code tool)
- `detect_dangerous_command()` — approval.py:2054

**Regression introduced by:** commit `3988c3c24` (feat: shell hooks — wire shell scripts as Hermes hook callbacks, v0.11.0, 2026-04-20). This PR moved `discover_plugins()` from inside `cmd_chat()` to `main()`, placing it before the `HERMES_YOLO_MODE` assignment. Before this PR, `tools.approval` was first imported during `cli.py` import (triggered from within `cmd_chat()` at ~line 1133), which happened *after* the env var was set at ~line 1118 — so `_YOLO_MODE_FROZEN` correctly read `True`.

**Why this bug was hidden until recently:** the bug has existed since v0.11.0, but was masked because Tirith was not always auto-installed. When Tirith is absent, `check_command_security()` fails open (returns allow), so only the narrower `detect_dangerous_command()` patterns (rm -rf, sudo, etc.) would trigger approval — and those are less common in daily use. Once Tirith is auto-installed (via `hermes update` or startup prefetch), its broader rule set (pipe-to-interpreter, script execution via flags, etc.) causes many more commands to hit the approval path, making the broken YOLO bypass plainly visible.

## Proposed Fix

Move the `HERMES_YOLO_MODE` assignment from `cmd_chat()` to `main()`, placing it between `parse_args()` and `_prepare_agent_startup()`:

```python
# main(), after parse_args, before _prepare_agent_startup:
args = parser.parse_args(_processed_argv)

if getattr(args, "yolo", False):
    os.environ["HERMES_YOLO_MODE"] = "1"

_prepare_agent_startup(args)
```

This does not weaken security: the hardline blocklist (rm -rf /, mkfs, fork bombs, etc.), sudo stdin guard, and user deny rules all execute *before* the YOLO bypass check and remain enforceable. The `_YOLO_MODE_FROZEN` import-time freeze design (PR #7994) is preserved unchanged — only the env var setting timing is corrected.

## Workaround

Set the env var before the process starts:

```bash
HERMES_YOLO_MODE=1 hermes
```

Or add a shell alias:

```bash
alias hy='HERMES_YOLO_MODE=1 hermes'
```

The in-chat `/yolo` command is **not affected** — it uses `enable_session_yolo()` (session-scoped, runtime set, PR #33931), which is independent of `_YOLO_MODE_FROZEN`.

## Related

- PR #7994 — introduced `_YOLO_MODE_FROZEN` import-time freeze (security hardening, correct design)
- Commit `3988c3c24` — introduced the regression by moving `discover_plugins()` to `main()` before `cmd_chat()`
- Issue #33925 / PR #33931 — similar `_YOLO_MODE_FROZEN` issue but for the in-chat `/yolo` command (different code path, already fixed for that path)
- PR #34032 — another proposed fix for the in-chat `/yolo` path (still open)

## Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [x] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

items.title: opencode-go + deepseek-v4-flash streams hang for 30–50s as APITimeoutError (direct httpx succeeds in ~3s)

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
## `opencode-go` + `deepseek-v4-flash` / `deepseek-v4-pro` streams hang for 30–50s and surface as `APITimeoutError` inside Hermes; direct calls and `openai-python` succeed in ~3s

### Summary

When the primary model is set to a deepseek-v4 reasoning model served by
`opencode-go` (`provider=opencode-go`, `base_url=https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1`),
every chat completion inside Hermes times out at ~30–50s with
`APITimeoutError`, even on a brand-new session that sends a single
`"hi"` message. The same deepseek models respond in ~3s when called
outside Hermes (raw `httpx`, or `openai-python` 2.24.0 with the same
keepalive `httpx.Client` shape). Other models on the same base URL
(`minimax-m3`, `minimax-m2.5`, `glm-5.2`) work normally inside Hermes.

This appears to be a regression introduced in the
`#58766` area of history (per our local memory notes) where
post-`#58766` `opencode-go + deepseek thinking models` started
hitting 50–75s timeouts. Earlier reports indicated the same code
worked on 2026-07-04.

### Environment

- Hermes Agent **0.18.0** (`299d5c660` on default branch)
- Python 3.11.15, Windows 10
- `openai==2.24.0`, `httpx` from `hermes-agent/venv`
- `OPENCODE_GO_API_KEY` set in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\.env`
- `OPENCODE_GO_BASE_URL=https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1`
- `model.provider=opencode-go`, `model.default=deepseek-v4-flash`
  (also reproduces with `deepseek-v4-pro`; `minimax-m3`, `minimax-m2.5`,
  `glm-5.2` on the same base URL are unaffected)

### Reproduction

1. Configure the primary model:
   ```bash
   hermes config set model.default deepseek-v4-flash
   ```
2. Start a brand-new chat (no prior history):
   ```bash
   hermes chat
   ```
3. Send a single message: `hi`
4. Wait. After ~30–50 seconds the agent reports:
   ```
   API call failed (attempt 1/3) error_type=APITimeoutError
   provider=opencode-go
   base_url=https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1
   model=deepseek-v4-flash
   summary=Request timed out.
   ```
5. Retries 2/3 and 3/3 follow with the same `APITimeoutError` at
   similar intervals.

### Expected

A streaming response in 3–5s, as observed for `minimax-m3` /
`glm-5.2` on the same `opencode-go` base URL, and as observed for
`deepseek-v4-flash` when called directly.

### Log fingerprint (from `%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\logs\agent.log`)

```
OpenAI client created (chat_completion_stream_request, shared=False)
  thread=Thread-XXX  provider=opencode-go
  base_url=https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1
  model=deepseek-v4-flash

# ~32s later, no chunk delivered to the agent:

OpenAI client closed (stream_request_complete, shared=False,
  tcp_force_closed=0)
WARNING agent.conversation_loop:
  API call failed (attempt 1/3) error_type=APITimeoutError
  provider=opencode-go
  base_url=https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1
  model=deepseek-v4-flash
  summary=Request timed out.
```

### What we ruled out

1. **The provider is healthy.** Direct `httpx` calls to
   `https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/chat/completions` with the same
   `OPENCODE_GO_API_KEY`, the same `deepseek-v4-flash` model, and the
   same `stream=true` payload return 200 in 3.0–3.4s.
   - 8/8 hot-connection requests (`max_keepalive_connections=20`,
     `read=None`): all 200, first byte at ~3.0s
   - 6/6 cold-connection requests (new `httpx.Client` per call): all
     200, first byte at 3.04–3.12s
   - Payload: `{"model":"deepseek-v4-flash","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"reply with one word: pong"}],"stream":true,"max_tokens":16}`
2. **`openai-python` 2.24.0 is fine.** Calling
   `client.chat.completions.create(model="deepseek-v4-flash",
   messages=[…], stream=True, timeout=1800.0, stream_options={"include_usage":True})`
   with a keepalive `httpx.Client(limits=httpx.Limits(20,100),
   timeout=httpx.Timeout(connect=15, read=None, write=15, pool=10),
   trust_env=False)` and `max_retries=0` returns the full stream in
   3.7–10s depending on prompt length (up to 50k input tokens tested).
3. **Other models on the same base URL work.** `minimax-m3`,
   `minimax-m2.5`, and `glm-5.2` stream correctly through Hermes in
   4–10s on the same `opencode-go` endpoint.
4. **Streaming was not disabled by us.** Setting
   `HERMES_API_DISABLE_STREAMING=1` did not resolve the failure
   (already tried before filing).
5. **Not a TLS / certificate issue.** Direct `httpx` calls to the
   same host succeed; failures are not preceded by `CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED`
   or `SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED` in the log.

### What makes the deepseek-v4 stream unusual

When reading the raw stream byte-for-byte we noticed two patterns that
do not appear with `minimax-m3` / `glm-5.2`:

1. Reasoning is delivered in a **separate `delta.reasoning_content` field**,
   not interleaved with `delta.content`. Concretely, for `"hi"` with
   `max_tokens=16`, we see ~17 chunks where `delta.content` is `None` and
   only `delta.reasoning_content` is non-empty, followed by one chunk
   where `delta.content` is non-empty and `delta.reasoning_content` is
   `None`, then a chunk with `finish_reason="length"` and `usage`
   including `completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens=16` (i.e. all
   16 tokens were spent on reasoning).
2. After the final `data: {... finish_reason="length" ... usage{...} }`
   line, `opencode-go` emits an **extra `data: {"choices":[],"x-opencode-type":"inference-cost","cost":"0.00001638",…}` line**, then
   `data: [DONE]`, and finally one more trailing line
   `data: {"choices":[],"cost":"0"}` with no `[DONE]` terminator.

We are **not** claiming these are bugs in `opencode-go` — we are
flagging them as distinguishing input the Hermes stream loop /
stale-detector has to handle.

### Suspect code paths in Hermes

- `agent/chat_completion_helpers.py` — the streaming loop in
  `_interruptible_api_call`, including the
  `_stream_stale_timeout` watchdog (~2855–2894) and the
  `last_chunk_time` / `deltas_were_sent` machinery.
- `run_agent.py` — `_build_keepalive_http_client` (line ~3888),
  `_create_request_openai_client` (line ~4074), and
  `_resolved_api_call_timeout` (line ~1186).
- `agent/agent_runtime_helpers.py` — `create_openai_client`
  (line ~1626) which injects the keepalive `httpx.Client` and
  pins `max_retries=0`.

Specifically, the **32–50s hang on a brand-new session** is the
strongest clue: with `_stream_stale_timeout` defaulting to 180s
scaled to 240s for `>50k` token contexts (and to a reasoning-model
floor in `agent/reasoning_timeouts.py`), the value being hit here
looks like the **`_resolved_api_call_timeout()` default of 1800s is
NOT what is firing** — something inside the OpenAI SDK is closing
the request at ~32s and surfacing `APITimeoutError`. It is also not
the same number on every attempt (logs show 32s, 38s, 50s on
different sessions), which suggests the value is environment-driven
(e.g. an inner httpx `Timeout(read=…)` set per request, or a
provider-side keepalive being killed).

### Requested help

1. Confirm whether the team can reproduce `opencode-go +
   deepseek-v4-flash` hanging inside Hermes' `_interruptible_api_call`
   while direct `httpx` works.
2. If so, is there a known fix / workaround? Locally we are running
   `model.default=minimax-m3` as a stopgap.
3. Is `_build_keepalive_http_client`'s 20-keepalive limit + the
   "thinking" stream shape interacting with the new
   `opencode-go` `inference-cost` post-frame a known issue?
4. The `agent/reasoning_timeouts.py` reasoning-model floor is the
   only place we see `deepseek` mentioned by name — does it know
   about `deepseek-v4-*`? If not, could that be why the watchdog
   fires at a non-default value?

### Workaround

Switch the primary model to `minimax-m3` (or any non-reasoning
model on `opencode-go`). This unblocks us today; we would prefer
deepseek-v4-flash once this is fixed.

```bash
hermes config set model.default minimax-m3
```

### Logs / repro script

We can provide a minimal Python reproducer that uses
`_build_keepalive_http_client` + `OpenAI(max_retries=0,
http_client=…, timeout=1800.0)` and reliably hangs the iterator
inside Hermes' sandbox, while completing in ~4s when run from a
plain Python REPL. Happy to attach on request.

items.title: [Bug]: fix(moa): reference models silently degrade on context overflow

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:cannot-reproduce
labels.description: Sweeper: could not reproduce on current main

items.body:
### Bug Description

When a MoA reference model's context window is smaller than the conversation history sent to it, the reference call fails silently and degrades the MoA turn to fewer references with no user-visible signal.

The aggregator is protected by ContextCompressor (trims history before the context window is exceeded), but reference models go through _run_reference → call_llm with no equivalent protection. A reference whose window is smaller than the aggregator's (e.g. kimi-k2.7-code @ 262144 tokens as reference, glm-5.2 @ 1000000 tokens as aggregator) will degrade first, invisibly, as the conversation grows.

What happened?
A MoA reference model whose context window is smaller than the conversation history gets a hard HTTP 400 from the provider ("The prompt is too long"), which _run_reference's try/except (agent/moa_loop.py:268-277) converts into a [failed: ...] label. The MoA turn continues with the remaining references, but no error, warning, or UI signal is surfaced — the only observable effect is that one fewer reference opinion appears in the aggregated guidance.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure a MoA preset with a 256K-window reference (e.g. kimi-k2.7-code)
   and a 1M-window aggregator (e.g. glm-5.2), both via ollama-cloud
2. Start a conversation and let it grow until _reference_messages() produces
   > 262144 tokens (or craft a single turn with large tool output history)
3. Trigger a MoA turn
4. The kimi-k2.7-code reference call returns HTTP 400:
   "The prompt is too long: 265540, model maximum context length: 262144"
5. _run_reference catches the exception, returns [failed: ...] as reference text
6. Aggregator synthesizes guidance from remaining references — no error shown

### Expected Behavior

Either:
(a) The reference's history is trimmed to fit its own context window
    (analogous to what ContextCompressor does for the aggregator), OR
(b) A visible signal (warning, status line, event) indicates that a
    reference model was skipped due to context overflow

Currently neither happens — the failure is completely silent.

### Actual Behavior

The reference call returns HTTP 400 from the provider:
  {"error":"The prompt is too long: 265540, model maximum context length: 262144"}

_run_reference catches the exception (moa_loop.py:268-277) and returns
[failed: The prompt is too long: ...] as the reference text. The aggregator
synthesizes guidance from the remaining references. No user-visible
indication that a reference was lost.

API-verified boundary (ollama-cloud:kimi-k2.7-code):
  ~250K tokens → HTTP 200, prompt_tokens=245860 (normal, no truncation)
  ~270K tokens → HTTP 400, hard reject (no silent truncation by provider)

### Affected Component

Agent Core (conversation loop, context compression, memory)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

N/A (CLI only)

### Debug Report

```shell
Option 1 — Trim reference history to fit (parity with aggregator):
  Before calling _run_reference, resolve the reference model's context
  window via get_model_context_length() and trim ref_messages if the
  estimated token count exceeds it. Mirrors ContextCompressor behavior,
  applied per-reference.

Option 2 — Surface the failure to the user (observability):
  When _run_reference catches a context-overflow error, emit a
  moa.reference_failed event with the reason, so frontends can show
  "Reference 3 (kimi-k2.7-code) skipped: context window exceeded"

Option 3 — Both: Trim when possible; surface when trimming fails.
```

### Operating System

Windows 10

### Python Version

3.11.9

### Hermes Version

2.1.0 (built 2026-07-01, content hash 8be25a82)

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell
Root cause — source-verified call chain with no context-length protection:

  api_messages (full history)
    → _reference_messages()      # agent/moa_loop.py:373
      # Fixed transform: drops system prompt, flattens tool_calls,
      # truncates individual tool results to 4000 chars
      # Does NOT check or trim against reference model's context window
      # Docstring: "preserve the whole conversation flow"
    → _run_reference()           # agent/moa_loop.py:176-277
      # Calls call_llm directly, no pre-flight token estimation
      # try/except at line 268 catches all exceptions → [failed: ...] label
    → call_llm()                 # agent/auxiliary_client.py:5811
      # No trimming logic (searched: trim/truncate/slice/compress — 0 hits)
      # _build_call_kwargs does not inject num_ctx for Ollama endpoints
    → provider API               # overflows → HTTP 400

ContextCompressor (agent/context_compressor.py:622) is attached to the
agent via agent_init.py:1657 and protects the main conversation loop only.
moa_loop.py does not import ContextCompressor.

num_ctx injection exists only in the main agent path
(agent_init.py:1787 → chat_completion_helpers.py:805), protecting the
aggregator, not references.

This is an asymmetry: aggregator has context-length protection,
reference models do not.
```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

The reference call path (_run_reference → call_llm) has no context-length-aware trimming, unlike the aggregator path which is protected by ContextCompressor. When a reference model's window is smaller than the conversation history, the provider returns a hard 400 and _run_reference's try/except silently converts it to a [failed: ...] label with no user-visible signal.

Related (not duplicates):

#56749: aggregator context-length resolution (PR #56758, open, aggregator-only)
#60272: reference models not informed about being reference models
#60282: reference models receiving tool definitions
#60064/60065/60068: custom_provider credentials not passed to references

### Proposed Fix (optional)

Option 1 — Trim reference history to fit (parity with aggregator):
  Before calling _run_reference, resolve the reference model's context
  window via get_model_context_length() and trim ref_messages if the
  estimated token count exceeds it. Mirrors ContextCompressor behavior,
  applied per-reference.

Option 2 — Surface the failure to the user (observability):
  When _run_reference catches a context-overflow error, emit a
  moa.reference_failed event with the reason, so frontends can show
  "Reference 3 (kimi-k2.7-code) skipped: context window exceeded"

Option 3 — Both: Trim when possible; surface when trimming fails.

### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [ ] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

### Summary

When the auxiliary LLM is configured with OpenAI-family models that require `max_completion_tokens` (e.g. `gpt-4o*`, `gpt-4.1*`, `gpt-5*`, `o1*`/`o3*`/`o4*` series and equivalents on direct OpenAI or compatible endpoints), auxiliary calls fail with:

```
Unsupported parameter: 'max_tokens' is not supported with this model. Use 'max_completion_tokens' instead.
```

The issue was first encountered while running the agent under Docker on a `linux/amd64` box.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Run the agent inside a Docker container on `linux/amd64` (the environment where the bug was originally observed).

2. Configure an affected auxiliary model (example in `config.yaml`):

   ```yaml
   auxiliary:
     kanban_decomposer:
       provider: openai
       model: gpt-4o
     # Also affects: triage_specifier, goal_judge, profile_describer, etc.
   ```

   You can also hit it by using one of these models as your main model (when auxiliary falls back to it).

3. Create a kanban board and place at least one task in the Triage column.

4. Run:

   ```bash
   hermes kanban decompose <id>
   # or
   hermes kanban decompose --all
   ```

Similar failures occur with `hermes kanban specify`, goal-related flows, and `hermes profile describe --auto`.

### Expected Behavior

The auxiliary `chat.completions.create` call succeeds (using the correct token limit parameter) and the task is decomposed/specified/etc.

### Actual Behavior

The call fails with a 400 error.

**Error from agent.log (inside the container):**

```
2026-07-07 14:54:59,308 INFO hermes_cli.kanban_decompose: decompose: API call failed for t_b6056d48 (Error code: 400 - {'error': {'message': "Unsupported parameter: 'max_tokens' is not supported with this model. Use 'max_completion_tokens' instead.", 'type': 'invalid_request_error', 'param': 'max_tokens', 'code': 'unsupported_parameter'}})
```

### Environment

- **First observed in**: Docker on `linux/amd64`
- Local development machine: macOS
- Hermes version (from inside the Docker container):

  ```
  Hermes Agent v0.18.0 (2026.7.1) · upstream f90a6d64
  Project: /opt/hermes
  Python: 3.13.5
  OpenAI SDK: 2.24.0
  ```

- Auxiliary model/provider: openai + gpt-4o (or o-series, gpt-5*, custom compatible endpoint, etc.)

### Root Cause

Several places obtain a client via `get_text_auxiliary_client()` and then pass a raw `max_tokens=...` argument directly to `client.chat.completions.create()`:

- `hermes_cli/kanban_decompose.py` (hardcoded `max_tokens=4000`)
- `hermes_cli/kanban_specify.py`
- `hermes_cli/goals.py` (both the judge path and `draft_contract`)
- `hermes_cli/profile_describer.py`

A helper already exists for this exact situation — `auxiliary_max_tokens_param(..., model=...)` (backed by `model_forces_max_completion_tokens`) in the auxiliary client utilities. These call sites were not using it.

### Related Issues

- #13901 (P1 High) — max_tokens/max_completion_tokens selection logic only checks host
- #34530 — Auxiliary context compression sending `max_tokens` to Copilot/GPT-5 models
- Other related reports around `_build_call_kwargs` and OpenRouter/custom endpoints

I searched open + merged issues and PRs before opening this.

### Additional Context / Verification

- The fix switches the four sites to `**auxiliary_max_tokens_param(...)`.
- Full test suite (`scripts/run_tests.sh`) was run. All tests for the modified modules and the `max_*_tokens` / auxiliary logic passed (unrelated pre-existing failures were present but did not touch these paths).
- A branch with the fix exists: `fix/max_completion_tokens`
- Docker image containing the fix (linux/amd64): `drhayt/hermes-agent:fix-max-completion-tokens` (git SHA baked in). This is the same platform/architecture where the bug was originally observed.

A PR will be opened shortly referencing this issue.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure:
```yaml
