items.body:
## Summary

`GET /` on the Hermes Dashboard returns a `500 Internal Server Error` when exactly one dashboard-auth provider is registered and that provider is password-only (e.g. `basic`, no OAuth flow). Accessing `/login` directly works fine and renders the password form correctly — only the root-path auto-SSO redirect is broken.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent version: `0.18.0 (2026.7.1)`, upstream commit `83016547`
- Dashboard bound via `hermes dashboard --host 0.0.0.0 --port 9119 --insecure --no-open`, additionally reverse-proxied through `tailscale serve` on HTTPS
- Auth provider configured: `basic` (username/password) — no OAuth provider (`nous`, `self-hosted`, etc.) enabled
- `curl -s https://<host>:9443/api/auth/providers` → `{"providers":[{"name":"basic","display_name":"Username & Password","supports_password":true}]}`

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure the dashboard with exactly one auth provider, and make it the `basic` (password-only) provider (`plugins/dashboard-auth-basic`).
2. Start the dashboard.
3. Load the root path `GET /` while unauthenticated (no session cookie).

## Expected Behavior

Either:
- The unauthenticated root request redirects to `/login` (the interstitial password form), same as it does when 2+ providers are registered, **or**
- The single-provider auto-redirect optimization only fires for providers that actually support an OAuth `start_login` flow.

## Actual Behavior

`GET /` returns HTTP 500. Server-side traceback:

```
File ".../hermes_cli/web_server.py", line 578, in auth_middleware
  return await call_next(request)
...
File ".../hermes_cli/dashboard_auth/routes.py", line 197, in auth_login
  ls = p.start_login(redirect_uri=_redirect_uri(request))
File ".../plugins/dashboard_auth/basic/__init__.py", line 230, in start_login
  raise NotImplementedError(
NotImplementedError: BasicAuthProvider is password-only; there is no OAuth redirect flow. The login page POSTs to /auth/password-login instead.
```

`GET /login` (bypassing the root path) works correctly and renders the password form — confirmed via `curl`:

```
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" https://<host>/           # → 500
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" https://<host>/login      # → 200
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" "https://<host>/auth/login?provider=basic"  # → 500
```

## Root Cause (from reading the code)

`hermes_cli/dashboard_auth/middleware.py`, function `_auto_sso_response()`:

```python
providers = list_session_providers()
if len(providers) != 1:
    # Zero → nothing to redirect to. Two+ → user must choose at /login.
    return None
...
provider = providers[0]
...
auth_login = f"{prefix}/auth/login?provider={quote(provider.name, safe='')}"
...
resp = RedirectResponse(url=auth_login, status_code=302)
```

This "exactly one provider → auto-redirect straight to it" optimization assumes the sole registered provider supports an OAuth-style `start_login()` redirect. It does not check `getattr(provider, "supports_password", False)` (the same flag `login_page.py`'s `render_login_html()` already uses to decide between an OAuth `<a>` button and a password `<form>`). When the sole provider is password-only (`BasicAuthProvider`), the redirect target `/auth/login?provider=basic` calls `start_login()`, which is intentionally unimplemented for password-only providers and raises `NotImplementedError` → uncaught → 500.

## Suggested Fix

In `_auto_sso_response()`, skip the auto-redirect (return `None`, falling through to normal `/login` rendering) when the sole provider is password-only:

```python
provider = providers[0]
if getattr(provider, "supports_password", False):
    return None  # password-only providers have no OAuth redirect target
```

This preserves the "skip the interstitial for the common single-OAuth-provider case" behavior while making the password-only case behave like `/login` was requested directly (which already works correctly).

## Workaround

Bookmark `/login` directly instead of the dashboard root URL. Confirmed this avoids the crash entirely and logs in normally.

items.title: bug: HASS_TOKEN in Tier-1 _ALWAYS_STRIP_KEYS means ha_* tools never activate in TUI/desktop chat sessions

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:risk-security-boundary
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may affect sandboxing, auth, credentials, or sensitive data

items.body:
## Summary

`HASS_TOKEN` is listed in **both** `_HERMES_PROVIDER_ENV_BLOCKLIST` (Tier 2 — conditionally stripped unless `inherit_credentials=True`) **and** `_ALWAYS_STRIP_KEYS` (Tier 1 — stripped *unconditionally*, even when `inherit_credentials=True`) in `tools/environments/local.py`.

Because `tui_gateway/server.py` spawns the `slash_worker` process (the one that actually runs the agent loop for TUI/desktop chat sessions) via:

```python
# tui_gateway/server.py:299
env = hermes_subprocess_env(inherit_credentials=True)
```

...specifically so it inherits tool/provider credentials, `HASS_TOKEN` still gets wiped by the Tier-1 strip at `hermes_subprocess_env()` line ~469-470, regardless of `inherit_credentials`. Net effect: **the Home Assistant smart-home tools (`ha_list_entities`, `ha_get_state`, `ha_list_services`, `ha_call_service`) can never activate in a TUI/desktop chat session**, no matter how `HASS_TOKEN` is set in `.env` or how many times the gateway/desktop app is restarted. The token only reaches the process if you `source ~/.hermes/.env` manually in a raw terminal and curl the REST API yourself.

This looks like it was introduced by the blocklist-expansion fix in #1264 (which correctly flagged `HASS_TOKEN` as a secret needing sanitization from *terminal/execute_code* subprocess environments, spawned via `_sanitize_subprocess_env`) but the same variable then got duplicated into `_ALWAYS_STRIP_KEYS`, which per the docstring in `hermes_subprocess_env()` is meant for secrets "no child Hermes spawns legitimately needs" (gateway bot tokens, GitHub auth, remote-compute infra secrets). `HASS_TOKEN` doesn't fit that category — the entire point of the token is for the agent's *own* tool calls (`ha_call_service` etc.) to use it, which requires the `slash_worker` process itself to have it in-process.

`EMAIL_PASSWORD` appears to have the identical problem for the email skill/tools, for the same reason.

## Repro

1. Set `HASS_TOKEN` + `HASS_URL` in `~/.hermes/.env`.
2. Restart the gateway (`hermes gateway restart`) and the desktop app fully.
3. Start a fresh chat session, ask the agent to call `ha_list_entities`.
4. The `ha_*` tools are absent from the schema (toolset gated on `_check_ha_available()` which checks `os.getenv("HASS_TOKEN")` at `tools/homeassistant_tool.py:345-346` — false, because the var was stripped before the worker process even started).

Verified directly by inspecting `/proc/<slash_worker_pid>/environ`: `HASS_URL` present, `HASS_TOKEN` absent, even though both are set in `.env` and the parent `hermes serve` process (spawned before the worker) *does* have `HASS_TOKEN` in its own environment.

## Suggested fix

Remove `HASS_TOKEN` (and likely `EMAIL_PASSWORD`) from `_ALWAYS_STRIP_KEYS` in `tools/environments/local.py`. They're already covered by the Tier-2 `_HERMES_PROVIDER_ENV_BLOCKLIST`, so the existing `inherit_credentials` flag semantics apply correctly:

- Terminal / execute_code subprocesses (via `_sanitize_subprocess_env`) — still stripped, addressing the original #1264 concern (agent shell commands / arbitrary scripts shouldn't see the raw token via `printenv`).
- `slash_worker` (`inherit_credentials=True`) — token flows through so `ha_*` tools actually work, matching documented behavior ("The `homeassistant` toolset is automatically enabled when `HASS_TOKEN` is set" — https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/messaging/homeassistant).
- Codex/Copilot ACP executors etc. (`inherit_credentials=True`) — same as above; these are user-blessed CLI executors and arguably shouldn't see it either, but that's a separate/smaller-blast-radius discussion than "the feature is completely non-functional in the primary UI."

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.18.0 (2026.7.1), local build with 4 carried commits
- Bug traced to `tools/environments/local.py` line ~424 (`_ALWAYS_STRIP_KEYS`) as of commit `75de0057b`
- Confirmed present going back through release tags to at least v0.11.0 via `git log -S'"HASS_TOKEN",'`

items.title: Gateway streaming TTS: let voice platform adapters consume the LLM token stream for clause-by-clause synthesis (closes the #47896 consumer gap)

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

labels.name: area/streaming
labels.description: Streaming responses: gateway delivery, provider wire

items.body:
## Problem

TTS on voice platforms is strictly turn-synchronous: the agent's full text response must complete before any audio synthesis begins. On a WebRTC/LiveKit voice satellite this imposes a hard latency floor of roughly 1.8-3.5s (LLM full generation + full-block TTS render) before the user hears the first syllable — regardless of how fast the TTS provider itself is.

We run Hermes as a family home assistant with a physical ESP32-S3 voice satellite bridged into a LiveKit room (gateway plugin `hermes-livekit`). Everything else about the loop is real-time (WebRTC audio in, barge-in works), but the reply leg is capped by the text-must-complete-first architecture.

## What already exists (this is a "finish the thread" request)

- #47896 notes plugin TTS providers **already define `stream()`** but dispatch never consumes it generically
- #58930 asks CLI voice mode to use generic `TTSProvider.stream()`

This request is the gateway-platform consumer for that same machinery.

## Proposed design

1. **Expose the token stream to platform adapters.** `AIAgent.run_conversation()` already streams deltas for UI display; allow a gateway platform adapter to register a `stream_delta_callback` consumer for the active turn.

2. **Clause-level chunking buffer** (gateway-side helper): accumulate deltas, emit on sentence/clause boundaries (`.?!;:` + comma-pause) for natural intonation rather than raw token spray:

```python
class StreamingTTSBuffer:
    split_pattern = re.compile(r'([.?!;:]\s+|,\s*)')
    def append_token(self, token): ...  # emits completed clauses
    def flush(self): ...
```

3. **Consume `TTSProvider.stream()`** (per #47896) per emitted clause — ElevenLabs and OpenAI both support WebSocket streaming synthesis with ~250ms first-audio.

4. **Adapter integration:** voice-capable adapters (livekit, discord voice, future) write returned audio chunks straight to their outbound track as they arrive. First audible syllable lands while the LLM is still generating the rest of the reply.

## Impact

Drops perceived voice latency from ~2-3.5s to ~500-800ms on WebRTC platforms, without touching the synchronous `text_to_speech` tool path used everywhere else. This is the difference between a walkie-talkie and a conversation for home-assistant deployments.

Happy to test against a real ESP32-S3 + LiveKit + ElevenLabs deployment — we have the full rig running daily and can provide latency traces before/after.

2. Disable relay by setting `relayBaseUrl` to `""` in `~/.hermeslink/config.json` (per the `hermes-link-pairing` skill instructions)
3. Run `hermeslink start` or `hermeslink daemon-supervisor`
4. Daemon crashes instantly

## Error Output

```
[daemon] daemon supervisor started
[daemon] Invalid URL
[daemon] daemon child stopped unexpectedly code=1 signal=null; restarting in 1000ms
```

## Root Cause

In `chunk-Y3KKN4J2.js` (compiled from `src/relay/control-client.ts`), line ~50845:

```js
if (identity?.link_id) {
    relay = connectRelayControl({
      relayBaseUrl: config.relayBaseUrl,  // "" when relay disabled
      ...
    });
}
```

The guard only checks for `link_id`, not whether `relayBaseUrl` is set. When `connectRelayControl()` runs (line ~49256):

```js
const wsUrl = new URL(`${options.relayBaseUrl.replace(/\/+$/u, "")}/api/v1/relay/link/connect`);
```

This evaluates to `new URL("/api/v1/relay/link/connect")` — a relative URL with no base — which throws `TypeError: Invalid URL`.

## Fix

Add a `config.relayBaseUrl` truthiness check to the guard:

```js
if (identity?.link_id && config.relayBaseUrl) {
```

This prevents `connectRelayControl()` from being called when relay is not configured.

## Environment

- `@hermespilot/link` v0.9.3
- Node.js v22.22.3
- Linux (Ubuntu 7.0.0-27-generic)
- Hermes Agent 0.18.1

## Workaround

Local patch applied to the compiled bundle — adding `&& config.relayBaseUrl` to the guard condition. This will be overwritten on npm update.

labels.name: dependencies
labels.description: Pull requests that update a dependency file

items.body:
## Summary

Running `hermes update` downgrades actively-installed newer package versions to stale exact pins from `setup.py`, silently regressing packages that the user (or a previous update) had upgraded to newer CVE-fixing versions.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent: v0.18.0
- OS: macOS 26.5.2 (Apple Silicon)
- Python: system Python in `~/.hermes/hermes-agent/venv/`

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Have Hermes v0.18.0 installed with a venv containing newer package versions (e.g. `cryptography==48.0.1`, `starlette==1.3.1`, `python-multipart==0.0.31` — installed via manual `pip install --upgrade` or transitive resolution).
2. Run `hermes update`.
3. Observe the pip output:

```
- cryptography==48.0.1
+ cryptography==46.0.7
- python-multipart==0.0.31
+ python-multipart==0.0.27
- starlette==1.3.1
+ starlette==1.0.1
```

4. After update, the venv has the older versions installed.

## Expected Behavior

`hermes update` should not downgrade packages below their currently-installed version if the installed version also satisfies the CVE/security constraint. Exact `==` pins in `setup.py` should either:

- Be updated to the latest CVE-fixing version, **or**
- Use floor pins (`>=`) instead of exact pins (`==`) so newer compatible versions are not stripped.

## Actual Behavior

`hermes update` reinstalls from `setup.py` exact pins, downgrading:

| Package | Was | After update | Pin in setup.py | CVE reason |
|---------|------|-------------|-----------------|------------|
| cryptography | 48.0.1 | 46.0.7 | `==46.0.7` | CVE-2026-39892, CVE-2026-34073 |
| starlette | 1.3.1 | 1.0.1 | `==1.0.1` | CVE-2026-48710 (BadHost) |
| python-multipart | 0.0.31 | 0.0.27 | `==0.0.27` | (in `web` extra) |

## Root Cause

`setup.py` uses exact `==` pins for CVE-mitigated packages. These pins were correct when written, but are now stale — newer versions (48.0.1, 1.3.1, 0.0.31) also fix the same CVEs. When `hermes update` reinstalls dependencies from `setup.py`, pip's exact-pin resolution downgrades the packages.

The `cryptography==46.0.7` pin is especially aggressive: it's a transitive dependency of `PyJWT[crypto]`, and 48.0.1 is a drop-in compatible upgrade that also fixes the referenced CVEs.

## Workaround

```bash
~/.hermes/hermes-agent/venv/bin/pip install --upgrade \
  cryptography==48.0.1 python-multipart==0.0.31 starlette==1.3.1
```

Must be run after **every** `hermes update`.

## Suggested Fix

1. **Update the pins** to the latest CVE-fixing versions (e.g. `cryptography==48.0.1`, `starlette==1.3.1`, `python-multipart==0.0.31`), **or**
2. **Switch to floor pins** (`cryptography>=46.0.7`, `starlette>=1.0.1`, `python-multipart>=0.0.27`) so newer compatible versions survive reinstalls, **or**
3. **Skip downgrades during update**: if the installed version satisfies the security constraint, don't force-downgrade.

## Related

- #53272 — `hermes update` does not reinstall active memory provider pip dependencies
- #59026 — Langfuse SDK silently removed from venv after update
- #39424 — stale `hindsight-client==0.6.1` pin

## Summary

After completing MCP OAuth for `robinhood`, tokens are saved and work for ~20 hours. When the remote server has a brief keepalive failure (transient network hiccup), Hermes reconnect logic fails and the error handling path **deletes valid OAuth tokens from disk**, requiring manual re-authentication.

## Reproduction

1. `hermes mcp add robinhood --url https://agent.robinhood.com/mcp/trading --auth oauth`
2. `hermes mcp login robinhood` — complete browser OAuth flow
3. Tokens saved to `~/.hermes/mcp-tokens/robinhood.json` (verified, 3 files present)
4. Wait for server keepalive to fail (or force one)
5. Attempt to use MCP tool → tokens are gone

## Log Evidence

```
2026-07-07 16:45:57 — MCP server robinhood keepalive failed, triggering reconnect
2026-07-07 16:46:27 — connection lost (attempt 1/5), reconnecting in 1s
2026-07-08 00:28:12 — OAuth tokens removed for robinhood
2026-07-08 00:28:12 — MCP OAuth robinhood: evicted from cache and removed from disk
```

## Root Cause

The keepalive failure triggers reconnection attempts. The reconnect fails (likely due to a transient server-side issue, NOT invalid tokens). The error handling path in `mcp_tool.py` / `mcp_oauth_manager.py` eventually calls `get_manager().remove(server_name)` which calls `remove_oauth_tokens()` → `HermesTokenStorage.remove()`, permanently deleting valid tokens.

The reconnect should retry with backoff and only delete tokens if the server explicitly returns an invalid_grant or the refresh endpoint rejects the refresh token. A transient connection failure should not be treated as permanent credential invalidation.

## Expected Behavior

- Keepalive failure → retry reconnect with backoff (works now)
- Reconnect failure → retry later, do NOT delete tokens
- Only delete tokens on explicit `invalid_grant` or user-initiated `hermes mcp remove`

## Impact

User loses MCP connectivity silently. No notification that tokens were deleted. User discovers the issue days later when they try to use the MCP and it fails. Requires manual re-authentication via `hermes mcp login` with a browser on the same machine — a poor UX loop.

## Environment

- Hermes version: latest (as of Jul 8, 2026)
- OS: Ubuntu 24.04
- MCP server: Robinhood Agentic Trading (https://agent.robinhood.com/mcp/trading)

items.body:
## Bug Description

`/compress` fails in the Desktop GUI with:

```
error: not a quick/plugin/skill command: compress
```

## Root Cause

The TUI and Desktop use different dispatch paths for `/compress`:

**TUI** — handles `/compress` via a dedicated `session.compress` RPC call (`tui_gateway/server.py:7696`), which directly operates on the session's in-memory agent and history. This works correctly.

**Desktop** — classifies `/compress` as `exec()` in `desktop-slash-commands.ts:151`:

```ts
{ name: '/compress', description: 'Compress this conversation context', surface: exec() },
```

The `exec` surface routes through `slash.exec` → `command.dispatch`. But `command.dispatch` (`tui_gateway/server.py:11479`) has no handler for `compress` — it handles `queue`, `learn`, `moa`, `retry`, `steer`, `goal`, `undo`, `snapshot`, and then falls through to the catch-all at line 11881:

```python
return _err(rid, 4018, f"not a quick/plugin/skill command: {name}")
```

## Affected Versions

Desktop GUI (all versions that use `slash.exec` → `command.dispatch` for `exec`-surface commands).

## Reproduction

1. Open Desktop GUI
2. Start a conversation and exchange several messages
3. Type `/compress` in the input field and press Enter
4. Observe the error message

## Expected Behavior

`/compress` should compress the conversation context, matching TUI behavior.

## Suggested Fix

Either:

1. **Desktop-side**: Change `/compress`'s surface from `exec()` to a dedicated action that calls `session.compress` RPC directly (similar to how the TUI does it in `ui-tui/src/app/slash/commands/session.ts:194`).

2. **Server-side**: Add a `compress` case to the `command.dispatch` handler in `tui_gateway/server.py` that calls `_compress_session_history()` and returns the result, similar to how `retry`, `undo`, and other session-mutating commands are handled there.

Option 1 is more consistent with how the TUI handles it and avoids adding more logic to the already-large `command.dispatch` handler.

## Environment

- OS: WSL2 (Ubuntu) on Windows
- Hermes: v0.18.0 (Desktop GUI)

items.title: [Bug]: macOS installer never acts as a launcher — .hermes-bootstrap-complete marker is only written by install.ps1

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

items.body:
### Bug Description

The macOS "installed → just launch" fast path added in v0.18.1 never fires, so every reopen of `/Applications/Hermes.app` shows the installer UI again instead of launching the installed app.

The fast path (`apps/bootstrap-installer/src-tauri/src/lib.rs`, the macOS-gated block in Install mode) calls `bootstrap::hermes_is_installed()`, which requires two things: a resolvable built desktop app **and** the marker file `<install_root>/.hermes-bootstrap-complete`. On macOS that marker is never created — the comment in `src-tauri/src/paths.rs` says it's **install.ps1** (the Windows installer) that writes it, and nothing in the macOS bootstrap pipeline does. So `hermes_is_installed()` is always false on a Mac, and the launcher behavior the code comment promises ("first run installs, every later run launches instantly") is unreachable.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. On an Apple Silicon Mac, run the notarized `Hermes-Setup` stub from `/Applications/Hermes.app` and complete the install (it succeeds: `~/.hermes/hermes-agent` is bootstrapped, the desktop app builds and launches).
2. Quit the desktop app and the installer.
3. Reopen `/Applications/Hermes.app`.
4. Observe the installer UI appears again. `~/.hermes/logs/bootstrap-installer.log` shows only `Hermes installer starting mode=Install force_setup=false` for each open — never the `hermes already installed — relaunched desktop` line. `ls ~/.hermes/hermes-agent/.hermes-bootstrap-complete` → no such file, even after repeated successful installs.

### Expected Behavior

Second and subsequent opens of `/Applications/Hermes.app` should hit the launcher fast path and open the installed desktop app directly, with no installer window.

### Actual Behavior

The installer UI is shown on every open, indefinitely. Users conclude the install "didn't take" and reinstall repeatedly (each one succeeds, none of them stamps the marker, so nothing changes).

### Workaround / verification of the diagnosis

`touch ~/.hermes/hermes-agent/.hermes-bootstrap-complete` — after that, opening `/Applications/Hermes.app` logs `hermes already installed — relaunched desktop; exiting installer` and the app opens directly, as designed.

### Suggested fix

Stamp `.hermes-bootstrap-complete` at the end of a successful bootstrap in the installer itself (e.g. the `complete` stage in `src-tauri/src/bootstrap.rs`), mirroring what install.ps1 does on Windows — that also keeps the marker's other consumer consistent (`hermes_cli/main.py` uses it to distinguish managed installs from dev checkouts in the venv health check).

### Environment

- Installer stub: `com.nousresearch.hermes.setup` 0.0.1 (notarized Developer ID build)
- Source checkout: `main` at 4d7f8ad (v0.18.2); first observed on v0.18.1, the release that introduced the fast path
- Platform: macOS (Apple Silicon, arm64)
- Affected component: desktop app installer (`apps/bootstrap-installer`)

## Description

MoA presets are no longer visible in the Desktop model picker dropdown. This is a regression introduced by commit `37a4cf90` ("fix: limit desktop model pickers to explicit providers"), which added `_filter_explicit_provider_rows` to inventory.py.

The filter explicitly excludes MoA:

```python
if slug == "moa":
    # MoA is a virtual routing mode, not an independently configured
    # provider. Hide it from explicit-only pickers unless it is the
    # current provider (handled above).
    continue
```

The Desktop picker calls `requestModelOptions` with `explicitOnly=true` by default, so MoA presets never appear — **unless** the user is already on MoA (current_provider === "moa"), which is a chicken-and-egg problem: you can't select MoA because it's hidden, and it's hidden because you haven't selected it.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure MoA presets in `config.yaml` with `active_preset` set and `enabled: true`
2. Open Desktop model picker (input box dropdown)
3. MoA presets section is missing

## Expected Behavior

MoA presets should appear in the picker when the user has configured at least one enabled MoA preset in their config. A configured MoA with presets and an active_preset **is** an explicit user choice — it should not be filtered out.

## Context

- Hermes v0.18.2 (2026.7.7.2)
- Verified: `hermes moa list` shows presets correctly
- Verified: `_moa_provider_row()` returns correct data
- Verified: `build_models_payload()` without `explicit_only` includes MoA
- The bug is specifically in the `explicit_only` filter path

## Suggested Fix

In `_filter_explicit_provider_rows`, treat MoA as explicitly configured when the user has enabled presets:

```python
if slug == "moa":
    from hermes_cli.moa_config import normalize_moa_config
    moa_cfg = normalize_moa_config(load_config().get("moa") or {})
    has_enabled = any(p.get("enabled", True) for p in moa_cfg.get("presets", {}).values())
    if not has_enabled:
        continue
    # fall through to kept.append(row)
```

Or simply remove the explicit MoA exclusion — the `is_user_defined` and `is_provider_explicitly_configured` checks already handle the general case, and MoA with configured presets is a deliberate user action.

## Related

- PR #53548 (previous MoA picker fix)
- Commit `37a4cf90` (introduced the filter)

items.title: Background task () fails with UnscopedSecretError when multiplexing is on

labels.name: sweeper:risk-security-boundary
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may affect sandboxing, auth, credentials, or sensitive data

items.body:
## Summary

When multiplexing is enabled (`multiplex_profiles: true`), the `/background` command spawns an async task that calls `_resolve_session_agent_runtime()` **outside** any `_profile_runtime_scope`. This causes `get_secret('OPENROUTER_BASE_URL')` (and any other per-profile credential) to raise `UnscopedSecretError`.

## Error

```
❌ Background task bg_134707_4da0e1 failed: get_secret('OPENROUTER_BASE_URL') called with no profile secret scope active
while multiplexing is on. This credential read must run inside a set_secret_scope(...) block (the per-turn / per-adapter
profile scope). Reading os.environ here would risk leaking another profile's value. See
docs/design/multiplexing-gateway.md (Workstream A).
```

## Root Cause

`gateway/run.py:13095` — `_run_background_task` resolves runtime credentials directly:

```python
async def _run_background_task(self, prompt, source, task_id, ...):
    # ❌ No profile scope installed — fails when multiplexing is on
    model, runtime_kwargs = self._resolve_session_agent_runtime(...)
```

The call chain:
```
_handle_background_command (gateway/slash_commands.py:2579)
  → asyncio.create_task(_run_background_task(...))    # fire-and-forget, no scope
    → _resolve_session_agent_runtime()                 # gateway/run.py:3738
      → _resolve_runtime_agent_kwargs()                # gateway/run.py:1836
        → resolve_runtime_provider()                   # hermes_cli/runtime_provider.py
          → _getenv("OPENROUTER_BASE_URL")             # runtime_provider.py:1074
            → get_secret("OPENROUTER_BASE_URL")        # runtime_provider.py:52
              → ❌ UnscopedSecretError (no scope + multiplex active)
```

## Compare with correctly-wrapped paths

**Per-turn agent run** (`gateway/run.py:16672`) — ✅ wraps in `_profile_runtime_scope`:
```python
async def _run_agent(self, ...):
    if not self.config.multiplex_profiles:
        return await self._run_agent_inner(...)
    profile_home = self._resolve_profile_home_for_source(source)
    with _profile_runtime_scope(profile_home):  # ← installs secret scope
        return await self._run_agent_inner(...)
```

**Cron job** (`cron/scheduler.py:3386`) — ✅ wraps in `set_secret_scope`:
```python
_scope_token = set_secret_scope(
    build_profile_secret_scope(_get_hermes_home())
)
try:
    ...
finally:
    reset_secret_scope(_scope_token)
```

**Background task** (`gateway/run.py:13095`) — ❌ no scope at all:
```python
async def _run_background_task(self, prompt, source, task_id, ...):
    model, runtime_kwargs = self._resolve_session_agent_runtime(...)  # 💥
```

## Suggested Fix

Add the same multiplexing guard as `_run_agent`:

```python
async def _run_background_task(self, prompt, source, task_id, **kwargs):
    if getattr(getattr(self, "config", None), "multiplex_profiles", False):
        profile_home = self._resolve_profile_home_for_source(source)
        with _profile_runtime_scope(profile_home):
            return await self._run_background_task_inner(prompt, source, task_id, **kwargs)
    return await self._run_background_task_inner(prompt, source, task_id, **kwargs)
```

This follows the established pattern used by `_run_agent` and the cron scheduler, ensuring credentials resolve from the correct profile's `.env` while preserving cross-profile isolation.

## Environment

- `hermes-agent` at commit HEAD (2026-07-08)
- Multiplexing gateway with `multiplex_profiles: true`
- Using OpenRouter as inference provider

I noticed a potentially confusing interaction where the repository level (house icon) and branch level (git icon) appear as separate items, yet both tooltips resolve to the same physical project path. ### **Related Issues** This appears related to **#53329** (duplicate lanes for non-git folders), which reports a similar visual redundancy issue introduced by the "Projects Paradigm" overhaul (#49037). The difference is that #53329 affects **non-git** projects (showing folder + "main" as duplicates), whereas I'm observing this behavior on a **git repository**. ### **Environment** * **Platform:** Windows 11 * **Hermes Version:** v0.18.0 * **Project:** Standard git repository with `.git` initialized * **Git status:** Single branch `main`, no worktrees ### **Observed Behavior** 1. labels.name: comp/agent

items.body:
### Problem or Use Case

Hermes agents cannot see which model is actually serving their responses. When the configured model fails (e.g. per-key 402 budget errors on OpenRouter) and the fallback chain activates, the switch is silent: the system prompt still names the configured model, the agent keeps believing (and telling the user) it is that model, and nothing in the agent's context reflects reality.

Real-world impact from my deployment this week: my orchestrator session silently fell back from anthropic/claude-fable-5 to deepseek-v4-pro mid-workday. The agent then confidently denied that Fable 5 had ever been used - while my OpenRouter billing CSV showed $2+ of Fable 5 spend that same day. Later the inverse happened: the agent claimed to be DeepSeek while actually running on Fable 5. For a paid orchestration setup where model choice = cost and quality routing, this breaks trust in every response.

A soft instruction like "announce fallbacks" in SOUL.md is not mechanically executable - the agent has no runtime introspection of the serving model. The only workaround we found is grepping ~/.hermes/logs/errors.log for fallback lines from inside the session, which is fragile and after-the-fact.

### Proposed Solution

Two complementary pieces:

1. Inject actual-model-served into agent context. The runtime knows which provider/model handled each completion. Surface it: refresh the "Model:" line in the session context block each turn with the actually-served model, or expose a zero-cost introspection tool (session_info) returning {configured_model, actual_model, fallback_active, fallback_reason}.

2. First-class fallback notification. When the fallback chain activates or recovers, inject a system-level notice into the conversation, e.g.: [MODEL FALLBACK: anthropic/claude-fable-5 -> deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro. Reason: 402 payment required]. The agent can then relay it to the user. Optionally a config flag like fallback.notify: agent|user|both|off.

Either half alone would fix the trust problem; both together make model routing fully observable.

### Alternatives Considered

- SOUL.md instruction to announce fallbacks: not executable - the agent has no source of truth about the serving model.
- Grepping ~/.hermes/logs/errors.log for "Fallback activated" from inside the session: works but is fragile, after-the-fact, costs tool calls, and requires terminal access.
- Asking the model "what are you": notoriously unreliable; models misidentify themselves.
The runtime is the only component that actually knows - hence a first-class feature

items.title: [Windows] Detached gateway crashes with `UnicodeDecodeError: 'gbk'` when a spawned child process emits UTF-8 output

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break or behave differently on native Windows

items.body:
[Windows] Detached gateway crashes with `UnicodeDecodeError: 'gbk'` when a spawned child process emits UTF-8 output

## Environment

- OS: Windows 10/11 (default ANSI code page = GBK / cp936)
- Python: 3.11 (CPython)
- Hermes CLI: 0.18.0 (release 2026.7.1)
- Trigger: gateway launched via `pythonw` (windowless / detached) — i.e. the normal Windows gateway service path

## Symptom

The gateway (and the TUI gateway thread) crash intermittently with:

```
UnicodeDecodeError: 'gbk' codec can't decode byte 0x85/0x80/0xae ... illegal multibyte sequence
  File "C:\...\Python311\Lib\subprocess.py", line 1599, in _readerthread
```

This is the background `_readerthread` inside `subprocess` that decodes the child's stdout/stderr pipe. It fires whenever a shell/git/tool command captured by the agent outputs any UTF-8 CJK text or emoji. The thread crash is caught by `threading.excepthook` and logged as `[gateway-crash] ... _readerthread raised UnicodeDecodeError`, which kills the gateway / TUI read loop.

High-frequency trigger sites confirmed in code:
- `tui_gateway/server.py` — `subprocess.run(cmd, shell=True, capture_output=True, text=True)`
- `hermes_cli/cli.py`, `hermes_cli/gateway/run.py` — every `text=True` pipe capture

## Root cause

On Windows, `subprocess` with `text=True` decodes child pipes using `locale.getpreferredencoding()`, which defaults to **GBK** on a Chinese-locale host. Any UTF-8 byte in the child output then raises `UnicodeDecodeError` inside `_readerthread`.

Hermes already has a UTF-8 hardening path, but it **misses the detached gateway process**:

1. `hermes_cli/__init__.py :: _ensure_utf8()` only sets `PYTHONUTF8=1` when it detects a non-UTF-8 *stream* (`if repaired:`). The `repaired` flag is set only when `sys.stdout`/`sys.stderr` are reconfigured. Under `pythonw` (no console) those streams are `None`, so the branch is **never entered**, `PYTHONUTF8` is never set, and the detached gateway keeps the GBK locale.
2. `hermes_cli/gateway_windows.py` builds the gateway's `env_overlay` with `PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8` but **omits `PYTHONUTF8=1`**. `PYTHONIOENCODING` only affects the three std streams — it does **not** change `subprocess` pipe decoding (that is governed by `PYTHONUTF8` / PEP 540).
3. As a result, the detached gateway process — and every child it spawns — decode pipes as GBK and crash.

(Note: `tools/environments/local.py` does set `PYTHONUTF8` on the *shell-tool* child env, but that only covers that one child; the gateway's own decode path and all other `text=True` spawns are unprotected.)

## Proposed fix

### 1. `hermes_cli/gateway_windows.py` — inject `PYTHONUTF8=1` into the gateway env (core fix)

`_build_gateway_argv()` (~line 797):

```diff
     env_overlay = {
         "HERMES_HOME": hermes_home,
         "PYTHONIOENCODING": "utf-8",
+        "PYTHONUTF8": "1",
         "HERMES_GATEWAY_DETACHED": "1",
         "VIRTUAL_ENV": _preserve_hermes_home_path(venv_dir),
     }
```

`windowless_gateway_restart_spec()` (~line 869):

```diff
     env_overlay: dict[str, str] = {
         "PYTHONIOENCODING": "utf-8",
+        "PYTHONUTF8": "1",
         "HERMES_GATEWAY_DETACHED": "1",
         "VIRTUAL_ENV": str(venv_dir),
     }
```

### 2. `hermes_cli/__init__.py` — set `PYTHONUTF8=1` unconditionally on Windows (belt-and-suspenders)

```diff
-    # Only nudge child processes toward UTF-8 when we actually detected a
-    # non-UTF-8 locale. On a healthy UTF-8 host children inherit UTF-8 from the
-    # locale already, so leave the environment untouched (minimal footprint).
-    if repaired:
+    # Force child processes toward UTF-8. On a healthy UTF-8 host children
+    # inherit UTF-8 from the locale already, but on Windows the gateway is
+    # launched via pythonw (no console), so sys.stdout/stderr are None and the
+    # `repaired` branch above never fires -- leaving the detached gateway and
+    # every subprocess it spawns decoding pipes as GBK, which crashes on
+    # UTF-8 output. PEP 540 UTF-8 mode is a harmless no-op on hosts that are
+    # already UTF-8, so we unconditionally enable it on win32.
+    if repaired or sys.platform == "win32":
         os.environ.setdefault("PYTHONUTF8", "1")
         os.environ.setdefault("PYTHONIOENCODING", "utf-8")
```

## Why this is safe

- `PYTHONUTF8=1` (PEP 540 UTF-8 mode) is a no-op on hosts that are already UTF-8; it only forces UTF-8 where the locale would otherwise be legacy/GBK.
- Adding it to the gateway `env_overlay` fixes the decode path at the single process-boundary that matters, instead of patching dozens of `text=True` call sites.
- It matches Hermes' own existing intent (`hermes_bootstrap.py`, `tools/environments/local.py` already set `PYTHONUTF8` elsewhere).

## Verification

After the change, restart the gateway (`hermes gateway restart` / `start`). Confirmed locally:

```
[1] PYTHONUTF8 in _build_gateway_argv env_overlay = '1'
[2] child preferred encoding = utf-8 / utf-8 | rc = 0
[3] current process preferred encoding = utf-8
```

A child spawned with the gateway env now reports `locale.getpreferredencoding() == 'utf-8'`, so `subprocess` pipe decoding no longer raises `UnicodeDecodeError` on UTF-8 output.

## Suggested changelog line

fix(windows): force `PYTHONUTF8=1` for the detached gateway so child-process pipe decoding uses UTF-8 instead of GBK

items.body:
### Problem or Use Case

I'm trying to use Hermes TUI with slash commands that are meant to inspect state, such as /goal status and other status-like commands.

Currently, some status/query commands feel tightly coupled to the active agent turn or current workflow. Instead of behaving like standalone control-plane queries, their output can feel appended to, merged with, or routed through the current conversation/task flow.

In Codex, commands like /status behave like independent runtime queries. I can run them at any time, and they immediately return current state information without becoming part of the active task.

I would like Hermes to provide the same mental model for status-like slash commands.

The expected behavior is: when the user runs a status-like slash command, Hermes immediately shows the requested state; the active agent task is not affected; the output is visually separate from the current assistant work response; and the command is not treated as user task input or steer text.

The current perceived behavior is: when the user runs a status-like slash command, the output can feel connected to the current goal, turn, or workflow; it may appear attached to the active assistant response; and it is less clear whether this was a standalone control command or part of the ongoing task.

This is especially noticeable with /goal status, but the same UX expectation applies to other read-only inspection commands as well, such as /status, /debug when used as an inspection command, model/runtime/context/usage/status inspection commands, and any slash command whose purpose is to read state rather than modify the task.

This is mostly a UX and command-routing issue. Status-like slash commands should feel like read-only control-plane queries, not part of the conversation or task stream.

### Proposed Solution

Make status-like slash commands behave as standalone, non-invasive control-plane queries in TUI/Desktop.

Status-like slash commands should return immediately with the requested state. Their output should be visually separated from active assistant messages. Their output should not be appended to the current agent work response. They should not be interpreted as steer text or user task input, even when the agent is busy. They should not trigger a new model turn unless the command explicitly requires one. They should not affect the active goal, continuation loop, current agent execution, or conversation task state. They should be safe to run while another task is active.

For example, /goal status could render as a compact system/control message showing the current goal state, active/inactive state, goal text, iteration count, last judge result, and next action. If no goal is active, it could simply return that no active goal exists.

Similarly, /status or other runtime inspection commands could render as standalone control output showing current model, provider, context usage, session ID, runtime state, or other relevant metadata.

The exact output format is less important than the interaction model. These commands should behave like control-plane queries rather than conversation messages.

A better long-term UI could include persistent status strips or panels above the composer, such as a small goal status strip and a runtime status strip. However, even if a persistent UI is added, slash commands like /goal status and /status should still return clean standalone output.

items.title: onboarding: mark_seen races with save_config - loses writes, bypasses normalization, can produce invalid config
items.body:
## Bug Description

`agent/onboarding.py`'s `mark_seen()` writes to `~/.hermes/config.yaml` through a completely independent code path from `save_config()` in `hermes_cli/config.py`, with no lock coordination, no normalization pipeline, and no env-ref-template preservation.

## Root Cause

`mark_seen()` does a full read-modify-write cycle on `config.yaml` but **does not acquire `_CONFIG_LOCK`** (the RLock that `save_config`/`read_raw_config`/`load_config` all synchronize on). This creates five distinct problems:

### 1. TOCTOU race with `save_config` (highest severity)

```
Process A (mark_seen):  yaml.safe_load(f)  ->  add flag  ->  atomic_yaml_write(cfg)
Process B (save_config):  [acquires _CONFIG_LOCK, normalizes, writes]          ^
                              writes stale config over B's changes ------------/
```

`mark_seen` reads the entire config, adds `onboarding.seen.<flag> = True`, and writes the **entire** config back. If `save_config` writes between the read and the write, the `mark_seen` write overwrites with stale data -- silently dropping whatever `save_config` persisted (model settings, provider config, credential pool strategies, etc.).

### 2. Bypasses normalization pipeline

`save_config` runs:
- `_normalize_root_model_keys()` -- moves root-level `provider`/`base_url` into `model:` section
- `_normalize_max_turns_config()` -- migrates legacy `max_turns`
- `_preserve_env_ref_templates()` -- protects `${VAR}` references
- `_secure_file()` -- sets proper permissions

`mark_seen` calls `atomic_yaml_write(config_path, cfg)` with raw `yaml.safe_load` output -- **none of the above**. This means a `mark_seen` write can reintroduce legacy key formats that `save_config` just cleaned up, causing structural inconsistency on the next `load_config`.

### 3. Cache invalidation gap

`read_raw_config()` caches parsed YAML keyed on `(mtime_ns, size)`. `mark_seen()` writes through `atomic_yaml_write` (tempfile + fsync + rename) which produces a new inode/mtime -- but `mark_seen` never clears the `_RAW_CONFIG_CACHE`. The gateway's `_load_gateway_config()` calls `read_raw_config()` and gets stale data, potentially showing onboarding hints **twice**.

### 4. No `_secure_file()` hardening

`save_config` calls `_secure_file(config_path)`. `mark_seen` does not. The atomic write does restore the original file mode from `_preserve_file_mode`, but for new or permissively-moded files the result may differ from what `save_config` would set.

### 5. Cross-process race (CLI vs gateway)

Both processes call `mark_seen` on the same `config.yaml`:

| File | Line | Flag |
|------|------|------|
| cli.py | 9896 | TOOL_PROGRESS_FLAG |
| cli.py | 11904 | OPENCLAW_RESIDUE_FLAG |
| cli.py | 12223 | BUSY_INPUT_FLAG |
| gateway/run.py | 4347 | BUSY_INPUT_FLAG |
| gateway/run.py | 9332 | PROFILE_BUILD_FLAG |
| gateway/run.py | 14485 | TOOL_PROGRESS_FLAG |

Two concurrent `mark_seen` calls can both read the old config, both add their flag, and the second writer atomically overwrites the first's changes -- silently.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start CLI and gateway simultaneously (or close enough that both hit startup onboarding)
2. Both call `mark_seen()` for different flags
3. One write silently overwrites the other
4. Flag never persisted; hint fires again next session

## Expected Behavior

- `mark_seen()` should either acquire `_CONFIG_LOCK` and route through `save_config()`, or use `atomic_roundtrip_yaml_update()` (already exists in `utils.py:232`) to write **only** the `onboarding.seen.<flag>` leaf without rewriting the entire config file.
- All writes to `config.yaml` should go through a single synchronous path.

## Proposed Fix

Two options (or both):

**Option A**: Replace the `atomic_yaml_write` in `mark_seen` with a call to `atomic_roundtrip_yaml_update(config_path, "onboarding.seen.<flag>", True)` -- writes only the changed leaf using `ruamel.yaml`, preserving comments, ordering, and all other keys untouched. Eliminates the race entirely because nothing else writes to that single leaf.

**Option B**: Have `mark_seen` acquire `_CONFIG_LOCK` and call `save_config()` instead of `atomic_yaml_write` -- ensures all normalization, env-ref preservation, and security hardening runs. Requires `mark_seen` to load config via `load_config()` (not `yaml.safe_load`) to get the properly merged dict.

## Impact

Any user running both CLI and gateway concurrently (the default setup with background gateway service) is exposed to this race. Lost writes include model settings, provider credentials, and onboarding flag state -- the latter causing hints to repeat.

## Affected Files

- `agent/onboarding.py` -- `mark_seen()` (lines 203-235)
- `utils.py` -- `atomic_yaml_write()`, `atomic_roundtrip_yaml_update()` (lines 180, 232)
- `hermes_cli/config.py` -- `save_config()`, `_CONFIG_LOCK`, `_preserve_env_ref_templates()` (lines 5854, 241, 5360)

## Environment

Every environment where both CLI and gateway are active. Observed in typical multi-process setups (gateway service + interactive CLI sessions).

## Bug Description

`tools/lazy_deps.py` pins `huggingface-hub==1.2.3` for the `tool.trace_upload` feature. However, `transformers` (pulled in by `sentence-transformers` for Hindsight local embeddings) now requires `huggingface-hub>=1.5.0,<2.0`.

After `hermes update`, `_refresh_active_lazy_features()` detects `huggingface-hub` as an active feature (because it's installed) and reinstalls it to the stale `1.2.3` pin. This breaks Hindsight's local embedding provider on startup:

```
ImportError: huggingface-hub>=1.5.0,<2.0 is required ... but found huggingface-hub==1.2.3
```

## Reproduction Steps

1. Install Hindsight with local embeddings (default `EMBEDDINGS_PROVIDER=local`)
2. Manually upgrade `huggingface-hub` to a version compatible with transformers (e.g. `1.22.0`)
3. Run `hermes update`
4. `_refresh_active_lazy_features()` downgrades `huggingface-hub` back to `1.2.3`
5. Hindsight API fails to start with the above ImportError

## Expected Behavior

`hermes update` should not downgrade `huggingface-hub` to a version that breaks other packages in the same venv. The pin in `LAZY_DEPS` should be compatible with the current `transformers` requirement.

## Actual Behavior

`huggingface-hub` is forcibly downgraded to `1.2.3`, causing Hindsight (and any other tool relying on `transformers`/`sentence-transformers`) to crash on startup.

## Root Cause

- `tools/lazy_deps.py:242`: `"tool.trace_upload": ("huggingface-hub==1.2.3",)`
- `transformers` (dependency of `sentence-transformers`) requires `huggingface-hub>=1.5.0,<2.0`
- `_refresh_active_lazy_features()` in `hermes_cli/main.py:7555` blindly reinstalls active features to their declared pins without checking downstream compatibility

## Suggested Fix

1. **Bump the pin**: Update `huggingface-hub==1.2.3` to at least `>=1.5.0,<2.0` (or a specific compatible version like `1.22.0`)
2. **Or decouple**: Don't pin `huggingface-hub` to a hard version if the only consumer (`tool.trace_upload`) works with newer versions
3. **Or make refresh smarter**: `_refresh_active_lazy_features()` should skip reinstall if the current version already satisfies the feature's runtime requirements

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.18.2
- Windows 10
- Hindsight v0.8.2 with local embeddings (default)
- `sentence-transformers` installed for Hindsight embedding provider

## Related Issues

- #44404 (same underlying mechanism: `active_features()` presence check causes false-positive activation and unnecessary downgrades)

items.title: build_channel_directory blocks the event loop with synchronous SQLite queries (Discord heartbeat stalls)

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

items.body:
## Environment

- hermes-agent v0.18.1 (2026.7.7), commit `f9eca7e15f1c2bfe5194aae5aa489af53c0a1a23`
- Discord gateway adapter, state.db ~3.7GB at time of observation (since cleaned up; issue is not size-dependent, only size-sensitive)

## Summary

`gateway/channel_directory.py::build_channel_directory()` is an `async def` invoked on gateway startup and on a periodic refresh (every 5 minutes per its docstring). For the Discord platform and for all "session-discovery" platforms, it calls synchronous, DB-querying helper functions directly on the event loop thread instead of offloading them. On a large `state.db`, the resulting blocking call takes long enough (10-40s observed) to starve the event loop, and discord.py's heartbeat task — which also runs on that loop — misses its window. This produces `discord.gateway: Shard ID None heartbeat blocked for more than 10 seconds` warnings and, in the worst observed cases, a gateway disconnect/reconnect cycle.

## Root cause (call chain)

`build_channel_directory()` (async), at the time of the observed failures, called these helpers directly (no `await asyncio.to_thread(...)`, no async wrapper):

- `gateway/channel_directory.py:124-127` (pre-fix) — Discord branch: `platforms["discord"] = _build_discord(adapter)`
- `gateway/channel_directory.py:148` (pre-fix) — per-platform session-discovery loop: `platforms[plat_name] = _build_from_sessions(plat_name)`
- `gateway/channel_directory.py:162` (pre-fix) — plugin-registered platform loop: `platforms[entry.name] = _build_from_sessions(entry.name)`

`_build_discord()` (`gateway/channel_directory.py:182`) itself calls `_build_from_sessions("discord")` at line 215 to merge in DM history, so the Discord branch alone hits the DB-backed path even though it looks like it's "just" enumerating guild/channel caches.

`_build_from_sessions()` (`gateway/channel_directory.py:281`) calls `_build_from_sessions_db()` (`gateway/channel_directory.py:293`), which does:

```python
from hermes_state import SessionDB
db = SessionDB()
...
rows = lister(platform=platform_name, active_only=False)  # -> SessionDB.list_gateway_sessions()
```

`SessionDB.list_gateway_sessions()` (`hermes_state.py:1812`) runs a plain, blocking `self._conn.execute(query, params).fetchall()` (`hermes_state.py:1844`) against `state.db` — a multi-way self-join with a `MAX(...)` subquery per session_key, which is not cheap once the sessions/messages tables are large.

The repo already has an async offload facade purpose-built for this: `AsyncSessionDB` (`hermes_state.py:6395`), introduced in `ea26f2271` ("feat(gateway): add AsyncSessionDB offload facade", 2026-06-29) and confirmed present in v0.18.1 (`git merge-base --is-ancestor ea26f2271 HEAD` succeeds on `f9eca7e15`). Its docstring states its exact purpose: "offloads each call via asyncio.to_thread so a blocking SQLite call never freezes the event loop."

However, `gateway/channel_directory.py::_build_from_sessions_db()` instantiates `SessionDB` directly and calls `list_gateway_sessions()` on it synchronously — bypassing `AsyncSessionDB` entirely. Grepping the current tree for other `list_gateway_sessions` callers shows the same raw (non-offloaded) `SessionDB()` + `getattr(db, "list_gateway_sessions", None)` pattern is also used in `hermes_cli/status.py:553` and `mcp_serve.py:149`; those are one-shot CLI/MCP-server call sites (not on the gateway's persistent event loop), so they are lower priority, but worth a pass if `AsyncSessionDB` is meant to be the sanctioned entry point for `SessionDB` from async contexts.

## Why this matters specifically for `build_channel_directory`

Unlike a one-off CLI invocation, `build_channel_directory()` runs repeatedly on the *same* event loop that also drives the Discord gateway connection (heartbeats, dispatch, reconnect logic). Any synchronous, DB-bound stall inside it is a stall of the whole bot, not just of the directory refresh.

## Reproduction / observation

1. Run hermes-agent with the Discord adapter connected and a `state.db` large enough that `list_gateway_sessions()` takes multiple seconds (observed 10-40s at ~3.7GB).
2. Let the periodic channel-directory refresh fire (or trigger gateway startup, which calls `build_channel_directory()` once immediately).
3. Observe discord.py logging `heartbeat blocked for more than Xs` around the same timestamp as the channel-directory refresh; in the worst observed instances this is followed by a shard disconnect/reconnect.

(Timestamps and exact log lines from the local environment are omitted here — they contain internal channel IDs — but the pattern is: `cron`/gateway log entries around `build_channel_directory` immediately preceding discord.py's `heartbeat blocked` warning, observed 2026-07-08 before state.db was pruned.)

## Suggested fix

Route this path through the async offload facade instead of calling the sync API directly, either:

- (a) have `_build_from_sessions_db()` use `AsyncSessionDB` (making it `async def` and awaiting the offloaded call), and make `_build_discord()` / `_build_from_sessions()` async accordingly, or
- (b) keep the existing sync helper functions as-is but wrap each call site in `build_channel_directory()` with `await asyncio.to_thread(...)`, which is the minimal-surface-area fix since `build_channel_directory()` is already the only caller that matters for the event-loop-blocking concern.

### Local patch (option b), applied and verified

```diff
--- a/gateway/channel_directory.py
+++ b/gateway/channel_directory.py
@@
+import asyncio
@@
             if platform == Platform.DISCORD:
-                platforms["discord"] = _build_discord(adapter)
+                # Sync build walks adapter caches and state.db; offload so a
+                # slow pass can't stall the event loop / Discord heartbeat.
+                platforms["discord"] = await asyncio.to_thread(_build_discord, adapter)
             elif platform == Platform.SLACK:
                 platforms["slack"] = await _build_slack(adapter)
@@
-        platforms[plat_name] = _build_from_sessions(plat_name)
+        platforms[plat_name] = await asyncio.to_thread(_build_from_sessions, plat_name)
@@
-                platforms[entry.name] = _build_from_sessions(entry.name)
+                platforms[entry.name] = await asyncio.to_thread(_build_from_sessions, entry.name)
```

Four call sites changed in total (the Discord branch, the per-`Platform`-enum session-discovery loop, and the plugin-registered-platform loop — `_build_from_sessions` is invoked from two of those three plus once internally by `_build_discord`, which is itself now thread-offloaded so its internal call is covered for free).

Verified against the existing test suite for this module:

```
$ python3 -m pytest tests/gateway/test_channel_directory.py tests/gateway/test_channel_directory_connected_only.py -q
41 passed in 0.78s
```

No test changes were needed — the existing suite already exercises `build_channel_directory()` through its public `async` interface, so moving the internals onto `asyncio.to_thread` is transparent to callers.

## Notes

- This is not fixed by the existing `AsyncSessionDB` offload work (`ea26f2271`, `0896facce`, `0a997aabb`, etc.) because those commits route *other* call sites through `AsyncSessionDB`; `gateway/channel_directory.py` was missed.
- Not size-dependent in principle — any sufficiently large or momentarily slow `state.db` (disk contention, WAL checkpoint, concurrent writers) can reproduce the stall; large DB size just makes it reliably reproducible.

items.title: Desktop/TUI cold-start stalls ~14s on GIL pressure during backend initialization — event loop stalled before first prompt

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery

labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break or behave differently on native Windows

items.body:
## Summary

On Desktop/TUI cold start (Windows), the Python backend's event loop stalls for ~14s during initialization — after `HERMES_BACKEND_READY` is printed but before the frontend can complete its "become ready" health handshake. The user perceives a 10-40s "loading sessions / data" delay, but the session DB itself is small (under 100 sessions) and SQLite returns `session.list` in milliseconds. The bottleneck is a synchronous GIL-holding initialization phase on the event-loop thread, not I/O.

## Evidence

Log timeline from a real cold start (timestamps preserved, paths/identifiers redacted):

```
15:35:05.913  Desktop cron scheduler started
15:35:09.103  ws accepted peer=127.0.0.1:8783
15:35:19.511  WARNING tui_gateway.ws: ws write slow (loop stalled >10.0s) peer=127.0.0.1:8783 — frame left in flight
15:35:19.897  WARNING tui_gateway.ws: ws write slow (loop stalled >10.0s) peer=127.0.0.1:8783 — frame left in flight
15:35:19.897  WARNING tui_gateway.ws: ws write slow (loop stalled >10.0s) peer=127.0.0.1:8783 — frame left in flight
15:35:24.492  WARNING hermes_cli.web_server: event loop stalled 13.8s (GIL pressure suspected)
15:35:25.666  INFO  run_agent: Loaded environment variables from .env
15:35:28.114  INFO  run_agent: OpenAI client created (agent_init) provider=alibaba model=ZHIPU/GLM-5.2
15:35:28.438  WARNING tools.registry: check_fn _browser_cdp_check returned False
15:35:28.514  WARNING tools.registry: check_fn _browser_dialog_check returned False
15:35:28.741  WARNING tools.registry: check_fn check_computer_use_requirements returned False
15:35:28.960  WARNING tools.registry: check_fn _check_kanban_mode returned False
15:35:28.970  WARNING tools.registry: check_fn _check_kanban_orchestrator_mode returned False
15:35:29.481  WARNING tools.registry: check_fn check_web_api_key returned False
15:35:30.863  WARNING tui_gateway.server: `display.personality` is set but `agent.personalities` is empty
15:35:49.443  INFO  agent.model_metadata: Could not detect context length for model 'ZHIPU/GLM-5.2' — defaulting to 256,000 (probe-down)
```

Key observations:

1. **The 13.8s stall is on the event-loop thread** (`event loop stalled 13.8s (GIL pressure suspected)` from the loop heartbeat watchdog at `hermes_cli/web_server.py:16870`). During that window the WebSocket cannot flush frames (`ws write slow` fires 3× — the backgrounded `gateway.ready` frame is stuck in flight).
2. **`session.list` is NOT the bottleneck.** It is already in `_LONG_HANDLERS` (`tui_gateway/server.py:227`) and runs on the thread pool. The session DB here has ~86 sessions / ~6600 messages / ~94 MB — `list_sessions_rich` returns in milliseconds.
3. **Agent build is deferred** to the first prompt (`_start_agent_build` at `server.py:1262`, `Thread-26 (_build)` appears at 15:35:28 — *after* the stall). So the stall happens *before* agent initialization, during the backend's post-`startup()` initialization window.
4. **The stall window (09.1s → 24.5s) sits between `ws accepted` and the first agent-build log line**, meaning something synchronous runs on the loop thread after the WS handshake but before the shell can process the first prompt.

## Root cause hypothesis

After `uvicorn.Server.startup()` binds the socket and `HERMES_BACKEND_READY` is printed, the event loop enters `server.main_loop()`. The first WS connection (`handle_ws` in `tui_gateway/ws.py:283`) accepts, then runs `start_background_mcp_discovery()` (which is light — it only spawns a thread). But the **loop thread itself** appears to get blocked by synchronous CPU-bound work triggered either by:

- module-level eager initialization in the import chain (e.g. `_mount_plugin_api_routes()` at `web_server.py:16545` runs `exec_module` per plugin, though this runs at import time, not on the loop thread), or
- the first batch of RPCs the Desktop frontend fires on connect (`setup.runtime_check`, `setup.status`, `model.options`, `session.list`, `projects.tree`...) — most are in `_LONG_HANDLERS`, but any *not* in that set run inline via `handle_request()` on the `to_thread` call, and a few of those do real work (config reads, credential file scans, model catalog parsing of the ~3 MB `models_dev_cache.json`).

The existing mitigations — loop heartbeat watchdog (`web_server.py:16852-16879`), disabled ws keepalive ping on loopback (`web_server.py:16806`), `_LONG_HANDLERS` routing — all target **steady-state** GIL pressure during agent turns. None of them address the **cold-start initialization burst**.

## Distinction from existing issues

| Issue | Scenario | Why this is different |
|-------|----------|----------------------|
| #58576 | `web_server` event loop stalls up to 51s under heavy agent work | Steady-state, during agent turns — not cold start |
| #53420 | `ws write slow` cascade during long terminal runs | Steady-state, during terminal ops |
| #60371 | "agent initialization timed out" after `serve` restart — GIL stall from MCP | Attributes stall to MCP background discovery; here the stall occurs with MCP discovery already backgrounded |
| #54928 | Desktop boot timeout too short (15s) | Raises the Electron-side timeout; doesn't address the backend stall that causes it |

This issue is specifically about the **cold-start initialization window** (backend ready → first prompt can be sent), which no existing issue covers.

## Reproduction

- Platform: Windows 10/11
- `hermes desktop` (or `hermes serve` driving the desktop app)
- A few plugins enabled (observed: `hermes-achievements`, `kanban`)
- Provider: a custom/DashScope endpoint (model `ZHIPU/GLM-5.2`) — the `context_length` probe-down adds a few seconds at the tail but is not the primary stall
- Consistently reproducible on every cold start

## Expected behavior

Cold start from `HERMES_BACKEND_READY` to "first prompt sendable" should be under 5s for a <100-session DB. The event loop should never stall >5s during initialization — synchronous CPU-bound init work should run in `asyncio.to_thread` / the pool, not on the loop thread.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent: latest `main` (commit `f64e4f4`)
- Platform: Windows 10
- Python: 3.11
- Sessions: ~86, DB: ~94 MB

items.title: Bug: Interrupt message duplicated by _replay_output_history after terminal recovery

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

items.body:
## Description

When a user interrupts an API call (e.g. by typing a new message during a long-running turn), the 'Operation interrupted' message is displayed twice — once from the Panel render, and once from `_replay_output_history()` called during terminal recovery. If the terminal resizes (SIGWINCH) afterward, the message is replayed again each time, causing 7-8+ visible duplicates.

## Root Cause

Three functions in `cli.py` form the duplication chain:

1. `_recover_terminal_after_interrupt()` (line 4241) — called after every interrupted turn
2. Calls `_force_full_redraw()` (line 4216) — which calls `_replay_output_history()` (line 4235)
3. `_replay_output_history()` (line 2545) — replays all entries in `_OUTPUT_HISTORY`

The problem: the 'Operation interrupted' message is already displayed via Panel at line 12598-12607, and `ChatConsole.print` routes through `_cprint` which calls `_record_output_history` (line 2594). So the message is both displayed AND recorded. When `_recover_terminal_after_interrupt` triggers a full redraw, the recorded entry is replayed on top of the already-displayed message.

On terminal resize (SIGWINCH), `_recover_after_resize` (line 4360-4363) also calls `_replay_output_history()` when width changes, causing additional replays.

## Reproduction

1. Start a long-running API call (e.g. large context, slow provider)
2. Type a new message while the call is in progress → triggers interrupt
3. Observe the 'Operation interrupted' message appears twice
4. Resize the terminal window → message appears again
5. Repeat resize → duplicate accumulates (7-8+ visible copies)

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.18.2 (2026.7.7.2)
- Python 3.11.15
- Model: mimo-v2.5 (Xiaomi) — bug is model-independent, confirmed in cli.py rendering layer with zero model/provider dependencies

## Suggested Fix

Either:
- Skip recording interrupt messages in `_OUTPUT_HISTORY` (add a guard in `_record_output_history` or before the Panel display)
- Or deduplicate entries in `_replay_output_history` against what's already visible on screen
- Or suppress `_replay_output_history` in `_recover_terminal_after_interrupt` since the Panel already rendered the response

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Summary

A long-lived Telegram gateway session can reach the gateway hygiene compression path, log that compression ran, but still leave the live transcript unchanged. The next inbound messages then continue to hydrate a huge transcript and can appear to users as "message sent but Telegram keeps spinning" or trigger unrelated provider/model failures while processing a stale oversized context.

This was observed in a real gateway session after a user sent a simple Telegram DM and then `/reset`/test messages.

## Observed logs

Gateway hygiene repeatedly attempted to compress the same oversized session but did not persist a compacted transcript:

```text
2026-07-08 06:53:01,461 INFO gateway.run: Session hygiene: 467 messages, ~238,472 tokens (actual) — auto-compressing (threshold: 85% of 922,000 = 783,700 tokens)
2026-07-08 06:55:02,028 WARNING gateway.run: Gateway hygiene compression for session 20260708_012218_4fb3dc73 did not rotate or compact in place (no session_db on the hygiene agent) — preserving the original transcript instead of overwriting it with the summary (#21301).
2026-07-08 06:55:02,029 INFO gateway.run: Session hygiene: compressed 467 → 467 msgs, ~238,472 → ~238,472 tokens

2026-07-08 07:04:57,451 INFO gateway.run: Session hygiene: 547 messages, ~256,005 tokens (actual) — auto-compressing (threshold: 85% of 922,000 = 783,700 tokens)
2026-07-08 07:06:58,096 WARNING gateway.run: Gateway hygiene compression for session 20260708_012218_4fb3dc73 did not rotate or compact in place (no session_db on the hygiene agent) — preserving the original transcript instead of overwriting it with the summary (#21301).
2026-07-08 07:06:58,096 INFO gateway.run: Session hygiene: compressed 547 → 547 msgs, ~256,005 → ~256,005 tokens

2026-07-08 07:11:44,973 INFO gateway.run: Session hygiene: 573 messages, ~282,962 tokens (actual) — auto-compressing (threshold: 85% of 922,000 = 783,700 tokens)
2026-07-08 07:13:45,663 WARNING gateway.run: Gateway hygiene compression for session 20260708_012218_4fb3dc73 did not rotate or compact in place (no session_db on the hygiene agent) — preserving the original transcript instead of overwriting it with the summary (#21301).
2026-07-08 07:13:45,663 INFO gateway.run: Session hygiene: compressed 573 → 573 msgs, ~282,962 → ~282,962 tokens
```

Later, after a gateway restart, the session was still large enough that a trivial Telegram message got attached to an enormous context:

```text
2026-07-08 11:22:50,756 INFO [20260708_071847_f9025faf] agent.turn_context: conversation turn: session=20260708_071847_f9025faf model=gpt-5.5 provider=copilot platform=telegram history=326 msg='hello?'
2026-07-08 11:23:09,068 INFO [20260708_071847_f9025faf] agent.conversation_loop: API call #2: model=gpt-5.5 provider=copilot in=543111 out=298 total=543409 latency=18.2s cache=15872/543111 (3%)
```

The same incident also exposed local model-route errors in a MoA preset (`provider=moa model=default` resolving to unavailable Copilot slots), but the gateway bug is that hygiene had already been repeatedly failing to shrink/persist the oversized Telegram transcript.

## Expected behavior

When gateway hygiene decides a transcript is too large, it should either:

1. persist a compacted live transcript safely, or
2. fail visibly and avoid pretending compression succeeded.

It should not repeatedly log `compressed N → N` and then continue using the unchanged oversized transcript.

## Proposed fix direction

Gateway hygiene runs before a user turn and already owns the session binding, so it is safer to compact in place than to rotate the session id from a helper agent. Force the temporary hygiene `AIAgent` into in-place compression and explicitly bind its compressor to the gateway `SessionDB` before calling `_compress_context()`. This keeps the same session id, archives old rows through `archive_and_compact`, and lets `SessionStore.rewrite_transcript()` update the gateway JSON transcript without needing a compression-tip/session-split dance.

Also add a regression test that the hygiene helper is constructed with/bound to a real session DB and has `compression_in_place=True` before `_compress_context()` runs.

## Impact

- Telegram/Discord/Slack users can get stuck with a bot that appears to be "thinking forever" on trivial messages after a long session.
- Provider/model errors become more likely because every new turn rehydrates stale huge context.
- `/reset` and subsequent messages can race with a stale oversized run, confusing users because one message is discarded as stale while another appears to work.

items.body:
## Summary

Calling the `project_create` tool (which the TUI exposes to bind a session to a folder) returns success and writes the expected rows to `projects.db` / `project_folders` / `project_meta`. However, Hermes Desktop 0.18.2 shows **no visible change** in the UI after the call — neither immediately, nor after a full process restart. The sidebar contains no project entry, the active-project indicator in the top dropdown is unchanged, and the session list is not grouped by project.

This makes the feature **effectively a no-op on Desktop**, even though the data layer claims the project was created.

## Environment

- Hermes Desktop: **0.18.2** (build stamp `ac6dd59`, built `2026-07-08`)
- OS: Windows 10 22H2 (build 26200.8655)
- Install method: `bootstrap-installer` (Tauri-based, per `apps/bootstrap-installer/` source paths in the local snapshot)
- `HERMES_HOME`: `C:\Users\Administrator\AppData\Local\hermes`

## Steps to reproduce

1. Launch Hermes Desktop 0.18.2. Sidebar shows the default list (新建会话 / 技能与工具 / 消息平台 / 产物) with no project entries.
2. From inside a TUI/CLI session, call:
   ```
   project_create(name="Hermes Workspace", path="D:\Hermes-workspace")
   ```
3. The tool returns:
   ```json
   { "success": true, "id": "p_2280acb5", "slug": "hermes-workspace",
     "name": "Hermes Workspace", "primary_path": "D:\\Hermes-workspace" }
   ```
4. Verify the database was actually written (via the bundled `python`):
   ```sql
   SELECT * FROM projects;
   -- ('p_2280acb5','hermes-workspace','Hermes Workspace', ...,
   --  'D:\\Hermes-workspace', 1783518882, 0)
   SELECT * FROM project_folders;
   -- ('p_2280acb5','D:\\Hermes-workspace',NULL,1,1783518882)
   SELECT * FROM project_meta;
   -- ('active_id','p_2280acb5')
   ```
   → All three tables are populated. The `project_meta` row also marks the new project as `active_id`, suggesting Desktop is expected to consume this.
5. **Fully kill the Desktop main process and respawn it** (this is important — see "What I tried" below) to rule out any hot-reload/cache hypothesis.
6. Observe the sidebar.

## Expected behaviour

After step 2 (or after step 5), the sidebar should show a project entry representing `Hermes Workspace` bound to `D:\Hermes-workspace`, allowing me to click into a session that is anchored to that directory — i.e. the same session-scoped cwd binding that the TUI gets from `project_create` should propagate to the Desktop UI.

## Actual behaviour

Sidebar is **byte-for-byte identical** before the `project_create` call and after a full Desktop restart. (I diffed two screenshots and the user also visually confirmed: "没有什么不一样" / "no visible difference".)

The new process is verifiably a **fresh start**, not the same process that served the sidebar before the call — see "What I tried" for the evidence.

## What I tried (so maintainers don't suggest them)

- **Diffed screenshots before/after `project_create`** while the same Desktop process was running → no diff. (Not conclusive on its own: a running Electron app could just not re-render the sidebar.)
- **Killed the Desktop main process (`taskkill /F /PID 23976`) and observed the children auto-reaped** → confirmed by:
  - Renderer / GPU / network / utility children gone
  - 5-second later `Get-Process Hermes` shows brand-new PIDs: 6384 (main), 17084 (gpu), 33416 (network), 16456 (renderer), 4268 (audio)
  - New `--launch-time-ticks=1307749876511` (old: `1307190469658`)
  - New `--field-trial-handle=2084,...` (old: `2116,...`)
  - Three independent indicators that this is a fresh Electron process tree that should have re-read `projects.db` from disk on launch
- **Inspected the in-memory state via SQLite directly** — `projects.db` is populated, so the file is on disk and readable; whatever Desktop is doing on startup, it isn't reading this table into the UI.

## Suggested root-cause direction (not a fix)

Based on `AGENTS.md` ("desktop features are welcome and land routinely"), the most likely cause is that the **`projects.db` → Desktop UI binding is not implemented in v0.18.2**, while the Python-side `project_create` tool *was* landed (and writes the data the future UI will need). In other words, this is a "data layer ahead of UI" situation, not a regression.

A rough map of where to look in the source:

- `project_create` itself: probably in `hermes_cli/` or `agent/tools/` (whatever implements the tool registry entry for `project_create`).
- Desktop sidebar rendering: `apps/desktop/` — the React components that render the "新建会话 / 技能与工具 / 消息平台 / 产物" entries. None of them currently iterate `projects` / `project_folders` from `projects.db` on startup, or the new entry would have appeared after the restart.
- Desktop main-process IPC: needs a `projects:list` / `projects:read` channel that reads `projects.db` and pushes results to the renderer.

I am happy to open a follow-up PR for the renderer+IPC part if maintainers agree this is the gap — but I want to confirm the design first since `AGENTS.md` is strict about not bolting on raw env vars and prefers the existing `hermes tools` / `hermes setup` UX.

## Additional context (lower-priority, but related)

While diagnosing this I noticed two related issues that may or may not be the same root cause:

1. **`state.db → sessions.cwd` is sometimes NULL** even for sessions that clearly ran inside a project. Example: the session that created `D:\Hermes-workspace\hello.py` has `cwd = NULL` in `state.db`, while its sibling session that created `hello.go` (created minutes later, same directory) has `cwd = 'D:\Hermes-workspace'`. The on-disk files confirm both sessions were anchored to the same folder at runtime; the metadata just wasn't persisted for the first one. (See SQL: `SELECT id, started_at, cwd FROM sessions WHERE started_at > strftime('%s','2026-07-08');`)

2. **A user-visible workaround question this raises:** "How do I get files from different sessions to land in different directories?" Today the only answer is `cd` in the terminal before opening a new session, or `write_file` with an absolute path. If `project_create` + Desktop UI integration is the intended answer, that integration is the missing piece — and that's exactly what this issue is about.

## Reproduction artefacts I can provide on request

- `projects.db` snapshot (before/after the call) — already shown in step 4
- `state.db` rows for today's 4 sessions, including the `cwd` discrepancy
- Screenshot of the sidebar before and after the Desktop restart
- PowerShell transcript of the `Get-CimInstance Win32_Process` output for `Hermes.exe` pre/post kill
